data.description: I am a US trained Interior Architect and Sustainable Project Manager who founded Material Innovations Ltd in 2005. We represented 5-8 brands of interior design materials like LVT, Eco-resin panels, wall and ceiling applications with high reccled material content and marketed these products to my colleagues and suppliers locally and regionally in the English speaking Caribbean. In 2012, I was eager to reduce our carbon footprint, verred away from importation of product and started investing in locally manufactured or assembled materials for use in my designs. This is a tall order as most materials and products are made cheaper in the far East. So while we waited for our government to pass a plastic bottle recycling bill, I worked at an activist for zero waste living, composting collaborative and green design in both islands of Trinidad, which is more industry based and Tobago whose economy is based on Tourism. Precious Plastics has been on my "to do" list since 2017 or 2018 when I worked with Compostable Food Service packaging brands both foreign and local. I shared the video since V1 and reached out to Dave Hakkens when we built a shredder to use for bio-plastics. However, a site for collection and upcycling on a community level has not yet been properly developed on our islands and we are in desperate need of the model for our communities so that our government can follow suit. I have opted to use my property in the heart of the capital and the main high school district as the location for Precious Plastics Port of Spain for collection, a full workshop and retail outlet. It is my intention to encourage my residential community council of Cascade & Casablanca to do the same once we are complete. data.description:
Working out of a local nonprofit, A Reason to Survive (ARTS), we run a local community point to educate and bring the community together for this journey with precious plastic. data.description:
Our names are Sergey and Anna Yaroshevsky. We are from a small town called Tikhoretsk, in the Krasnodar Territory. We have been in business for more than 8 years, our main direction is a flower cybermarket, a large floral service with a cool team. In plastic recycling since 2022. The problems of ecology, thinking and awareness of the choice of each of us are something that has always worried us. And when we were faced with the fact that there are many problems in the field of waste processing, we realized that we should always start with ourselves. And for several years now we have been sorting our waste completely (especially plastic), making a choice in favor of eco-friendly products. And over time we came to the conclusion that we want to develop in this business and benefit the planet - to turn recycled plastic into new products. Our production workshop specializes in the creation of loft-style retail shelves (iron base + shelves made of recycled plastic). The most stylish, durable, practical. The first line of products is intended for flower shops: shelves in the refrigerator, floral table, gift rack, shopping island. There are also several reception desk designs in development for all areas of business. Ahead we plan to launch a series of outdoor furniture for ritual purposes (for installation in the cemetery), bathroom furniture.

We will be happy to help you make your business more environmentally friendly.
data.title: annaborohova

data.description:
We are prototyping a model for zero-waste operations and delivering recycling concept for villages in Tamil Nadu, India.

Based near the city of Madurai (10km) in a beautiful EcoPark covering 2 acres, we operate our activities within the responsibility of Antenna Trust, together with microcredit program to empower rural women and spirulina production. We work with NGOs and local villages.

After 10 months of ideas and fundraising, we are in the prototyping phase. We are testing our machines, discover the material, construct our team and find models that could work with our local conditions. There are 2 focus: education for children, and income generation for women. 

The next phase is to implement workshops, collection points in our surroundings and recycling units in the villages.
data.title: Antenna Trust Recycling Project

data.description:
Hi! My name is Antoine. I'm a french expat in Quebec, Canada.

My friends and I are at the very beginning of the long, honorable, and ambitious journey Precious-Plastic is proposing.

To be entirely honest, we just discovered the Precious-Plastic universe right in the middle of the Covid-19 crisis, while wandering around the marvels of the Internet 🙈

We realized after a while what kind of powerful potential Dave Hakkens and Team Magic have created. We have been immediately seduced by the idea of getting involved.

We were pretty surprised, at first, to learn that no one ever started anything in our region. Neither a workshop nor a community point. Not even a solo member.

I don't have a background in plastic-recycling volunteering yet (though many of my friends and mates do). But I am an entrepreneur and I have a little bit of resources (time, network, etc) to leverage for the sake of our ecosystem 😃

Some of us are also involved in all different kinds of charitable organizations and communities, which would be a bit long to describe here, but will be definitely of use 🙂

We are already actively working on creating a little community point in Quebec City, Canada.
I hope that, eventually, we'll be able to set everything up and run a complete precious plastic network soon!

Feel free to give us any piece of advice, if you think we could use some !
Or connect with us, on discord, social network or email (or whatever else). It's always nice to chat and hear other stories!

Peace 🤙
Team Québec 🍁⚜️
data.title: Precious Plastic Quebec City

data.description:
I Upcycle and recycle HDPE and LDPE plastic bags into materials that are then made into backpacks and every day accessories.
Aoracreo is the name for my brand and working space, where i collect, sort and process plastics.

Aoracreo started back in 2011 with the goal of making my art and design sustainable, as well as making a living from what I could do with my own hands. Now, after 9 years of developing the materials, working methods and new products I have been able to develop a sustainable business that is my full time job by using readily available tech (Iron, baking paper and sandwich press) to process over 10 tonnes of plastic.

Since the Plastic monster is threatening all of us, my main goal is to share what i have learned so everyone else can see the potential of plastics and how little is needed to learn and understand plastics, and to be able to transform the unwanted into the most beautiful products.
data.title: AORACREO

data.description:
Intro:

Project: Aurora is the temporary name of a self-funded plastic recycling workspace run by Phoenix and Levi. We are hoping to create a mixed workspace, and eventually be able to take on large-scale projects. We have an area for a workspace, but are waiting on funding in order to start processing and selling high-quality and beautiful, useful products. 


Engagement: 

We will be engaging with and helping the Precious Plastic community as much as possible. All of our first moulds will be bought using the Bazaar, we will be selling extra raw materials back to the community at a low price, and we will be providing updates and tutorials online and sharing them with this community! Eventually we will be creating our own moulds and selling them on the bazaar along with some of our products.


Plans:

We will be focusing as much as possible on efficient production, allowing us to take more time finishing our products without sacrificing production time and increasing price. 

We eventually want to grow our business to include multiple focused locations, one or two storefronts, R&D development spaces, and community outreach programs to help others with similar goals. We hope to massively increase plastic recycling workspaces in our local area as much as possible. The team at Precious Plastic main gave us all the ability to create a better world, and we hope to do our part in building towards that goal. And of course, we'll have fun doing it!


How to Say Hello!

Discord: Project Aurora#3018

(Note: if you reach out to us, it will most likely be Phoenix responding. Feel free to chat, ask questions, tag us in social media, or just say hello!)
data.title: Project: Aurora

data.description:
If a joinery transforms wood into interesting pieces, we at Arte 8 define ourselves as a "plasticery": a unique workshop that transforms discarded post-consumer plastic into furniture, coverings, installations, decorative objects and even works of art.

The plastic we collect comes from residential and industrial use or from the voluntary collection of incorrectly discarded waste in the environment.

Through ecological beach monitoring work, I saw first-hand the impact of plastic on the Brazilian coast, and so I decided to found Arte 8 Reciclagem as a tool to spread the message that we are damaging our world with excessive plastic consumption, as well as wasting a very versatile material with products that are often discarded within a short time of use.

Since 2020, I've been trying to share my knowledge to motivate people to recycle, whether it's sorting waste correctly or collecting or transforming and selling what we call 'rubbish'.

Faced with the current challenges, I see the circular economy as fundamental to a socially and environmentally just world!

data.description:
The Artesanato Sustentável Lajeado project aims to preserve the environment and provide a different destination for waste. Its main activity consists of transforming plastic waste into useful and durable products. Plastic waste from cleaning materials such as bleach and soap bottles, pet bottle caps, buckets, hangers and even car accessories will be reused, as they can be recycled at high temperatures.




The main people responsible for carrying out these tasks are elderly people from the Lajeado Living Centre and the Association of Women Artisans and Entrepreneurs (AMAE). The workshop to make the handicrafts with the elderly was led by artisan Felipe Cazé, founder of Arte 8 Reciclagem, from São Paulo.



As well as receiving theoretical information about the process of making handicrafts using plastic, the elderly are trained to operate the machines and grind the plastic in order to produce personalised handicrafts. Coasters, keyrings, trays and even stools can be created from the recycled material.

data.description:
The Fàbrica del Sol Fab Lab is a public service that empowers members of the public in the use of new digital manufacturing technologies. Within the Fab Lab Network, the actions of this facility are based on sustainability.

The fab lab is located inside Fàbrica del Sol, a City Council building listed as a cultural asset of local interest. The building, which was originally built as part of the Fàbrica Catalana de Gas company’s headquarters, was refurbished to embody the transition from an old industrial culture to a new approach to the use of technologies based on knowledge and respect for the natural energy, matter and water cycles, of which we all form a part.

This further promotes the development at Fàbrica del Sol of projects to help improve people’s quality of life in the area of energy self-sufficiency, as well as projects linked to the circular economy.

Any project can be redesigned from the point of view of sustainability by means of eco-design and energy saving criteria. These might include, for example, avoiding buying materials to make the projects, as reusing materials helps prevent waste and turns it into a new resource

The facility features an open-plan area, with 3D printers, digital embroidery and sewing machines, a laminator and a vinyl stamping machine, facilitating collaborative work, where exhibitions and manufacturing and training workshops can be held. It also includes a Workshop Space where you can find large-format manufacturing technologies, such as a laser cutting machine, a CNC miller, an electric mitre saw, a plastic injector and much more.
data.title: Ateneu de Fabricació La Fàbrica del Sol

data.description:
Athens Makerspace is a young non-profit organisation, founded in March
2016. Ιt is a physical space that provides public access to a variety of tools
and equipment in both traditional and digital technologies such as 3D
printing, laser cutting, woodworking, sewing, electronics, cnc and many
more. It is a place for those who love craftsmanship, to network and turn their
ideas into reality.
Our Precious Plastic Lab focuses on teaching the
participants how to reuse plastic waste, starting with bottle
caps and turn them into new products. Plastic caps are the
most useful kind of plastic for our machines and at the same
time the least recyclable.
We have ran more than 30 educational seminars for
children and adults. The participants learn about plastic
pollution and how to distinct and separate different kinds of
plastic. Then they are trained in the operation of machines
that crush, heat, and melt the plastic into molds to create new products. For the purposes of the
Precious Plastic lab we design molds using the innovative applications of Athens Makerspace
digital fabrication machines.

data.description: In Elmina, the central part of  Ghana, a dedicated team at Buy Food with Plastic (BFWP) started in 2021 is on a mission to address two pressing issues - Plastic Pollution and Extreme Hunger. I am Ato Arhin, a passionate individual, advocating for sustainability and responsible production and consumption. As a  local organization one of our flagship initiatives involves the systematic collection of plastic waste. We've deployed a tricycle that travels through various neighborhoods, encouraging households to participate in our cause. We have Helpers and volunteers helping this cause. The tricycle serves as a mobile collection unit, making it convenient for individuals to dispose of their stored plastic specifically HDPE, PP,PET and plastic Sachets responsibly. This initiative not only promotes environmental cleanliness but also provides a tangible solution to the growing problem of Plastic Pollution in our communities. Understanding the importance of community engagement, BFWP organizes regular impactful events every month in villages in and around Elmina in Ghana. These events serve a dual purpose – educating the community on the adverse effects of plastic pollution and introducing our unique plastic payment system.  During these events, we encourage inhabitants to exchange their collected plastic waste for food. This innovative approach not only incentivizes responsible waste disposal but also addresses the issue of Extreme Hunger. The positive response from the communities demonstrate the effectiveness of merging sustainability with social impact.   The collected plastics are transported to our manufacturing facility in Elmina, where our dedicated team meticulously sorts them into different types and colors. The Local team comprises 25 Helpers/Volunteers a four full time paid staff - Country Manager, An accountant, Recycling Specialist and a General Secretary. In a community  event, we collect an average of about 7000 plastics; including PET, HDPE, PP and Sachets.
data.title: Ato

data.description:
Waste plastic, the infamous star of pollution, is in fact the main ingredient for our designs. We do not like to see this beautiful material with an almost infinite life being used so carelessly. In single-use products, plastics lose their value and even worse they threaten the health of our planet. We explore the beauty within waste plastics through design experiments, giving plastics the life and purpose they deserve. As we create, more and more plastic is rescued from the landfills and sent to your lovely hands for a full and happy life.

Let's talk about our history a little. We are three architects from very similar pasts. We completed our bachelors degree in Istanbul Bilgi University, then did our masters in Institute for Advanced Architecture of Catalonia (Iaac) in Barcelona.

We started a company called The Back Lab with two other friends from IaaC, The Back Lab was a company focusing on digital fabrication and computational design. Upon winning the first prize in an international competition called Destination Zero (held by the British Council) we decided to focus more on the plastic waste and founded Studio Blai in the fall of 2021. Now we work together with Döngüsel İşler Atölyesi (DIA) and the Horizon 2020 project by the European Union (Pop Machina). We are also a part of the Precious Plastic Community.
data.title: Studio Blai

data.description:
Chako is a social, creative and environmental enterprise operating from Mwanakwarekwe, Zanzibar. Founded in 2010, we train uneducated and unemployed young men and women to create handcrafted, upcycled items from waste, i.e. glass bottles, paper beads and dhow sails (a typical Arabic style local boat). We train this youth for employment and self-employment. 

Every year thousands of tourists visit the tiny island Zanzibar, a pearl in the Indian Ocean. While we always appreciate our guests and the economic support they bring through tourism, they also cause a lot of waste. We are a successful enterprise in upcycling glass, and see the critical demand for upcycling plastics. Reducing the amount of plastic waste is critical for the (marine) environment of this beautiful archipelago. Since 2020 we have started our plastic recycling workplace.

Our mission is to foster social, environmental and economic opportunities on the island of Zanzibar by enabling local artisans to preserve their craft, explore their creativity, and live a more sustainable life, while reducing the waste on the island. 

We act by educating, training, employing and seeking opportunities. Our developments in plastic waste management create multiple economic opportunities for craftsmen, waste collection, trainers, designers and brings environmental solutions for Zanzibar. We keep our focus on recycling and upcycling of what used to be waste into beautiful luxurious interior items, souvenirs and accessories which are sold to the tourists and tourism businesses in Zanzibar.
data.title: Chako Zanzibar

data.description:
Hello,
My name is Harold Sokyrka. I am the president of Kwik BagIt Products International. I am super excited to be a new member of Precious Plastic and I hope that I can be of assistance to all of the members.
I am an innovator from Saskatoon Canada. For the past 3 years, I have been researching the problems that are plaguing the Waste Management MRF facilities and Beverage Companies. I am now ready to launch the “ground-breaking” Patent Pending "System" that I have developed called the "Kwik BagIt Closed-Loop Rewards Recycling System".

The "System" is successfully retrieving over 80% of valuable recycled material from households and commercial businesses before it enters the MRF and Municipal Landfills. It prevents co-mingling and contamination & sends recyclable material directly to the re-processors. This will help to make these businesses more profitable and successful.  
This is a "game-changer" and a possible solution to the problems facing all stakeholders who are striving toward New Zero Projections.

With today's issues of rising inflation, increasing gas prices, and lack of understanding of the intrinsic value of recycled material, the "System" will be able to significantly reduce the amount of unnecessary plastic, glass, and metal that are plugging up our landfills and it will provide an incentive for the public to get involved in a rewarding method of proper recycling.
This link will give you a brief description of the "System"
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uYfPm62e42g

I am seeking distributors in your part of the world and if you are interested in forming a joint venture please contact me
 at my e-mail: info.bestwaytorecycle.com to arrange a Zoom meeting or contact me on What’s AP at +1-306-717-3895.
Thanks, I hope to hear from you.  Harold Sokyrka
#Reduce #Reuse #Recycle #NowGetRewarded
#recyclingmatters #Sustainability #Circulareconomy #PreciousPlastic

data.description: Beyond Precious Plastic would like to do just a bit more than only working with good recyclable plastic waste. We also would like to educate old and young about plastic and plastic pollution. Also guiding them how to start a workspace, community center, and so on. And we would like to pin point out it's not a game, it's a very serious recycling process, that involves this wonderful but at the same time hazardous material. We also contact companies how they can do better with their waste or with their plastic packaging. After all, that is where all nightmare begins with plastic. But that is just the tip of the iceberg, packaging. There are so many other arias where this went wrong, actually almost all branches. There is so much to do when it comes to plastic, but we are convinced, the best starting point to stop this madness is at individual level. We are based in The Netherlands, but we also come to Germany, Austria and all European countries as well. Our dream is also to start helping other nations also around the world. And right now, we are also doing it, like The Caribbeans, Nepal and we are planning to do that at The Maldives as well. It's very very needed. Our e-mail address is: santron@planet.nl

data.description:
Bin IT Right is a garbage management company whose only ambition is to respect every discarded material and up/recycle it. The dream is of a garbage-free world devoid of landfills.

The name Bin IT Right refers to the concept of putting the right materials into right bins, thus changing the way people look at materials which are not of use as they know it and learn the value of waste. We aim to create value for materials that are seemingly at the end of their life-cycles by working in collaboration with existing systems as well as by addressing the issues of mainstream recycling in India.

Bin IT Right’s social media campaign, ‘#binitrightchallenge (Bin IT Right Challenge) educates people about waste segregation and helps them in understanding how the waste that they are generating can become part of a circular economy rather than clogging landfills and oceans.

Bin IT Right targets to reduce un-used materials going to dumping yard. In our everyday life, we neglect recyclable materials, hence creating unnecessary pollution of our natural resources. Small steps at the individual level can become a big part of the solution towards this problem and this is what we work towards. As individuals, it’s very difficult to get a grip on these neglected materials but if we segregate it further individually and collect it as a collective group with the necessary support systems then it becomes easier to manage all kinds of waste responsibly.

Any material can turn into a resource whether it is a food packaging, stationery or anything else that is put in a dustbin. It is this awareness that we are trying to create by encouraging people to respect all kinds of materials and look at it with a sense of responsibility.
data.title: binitright

data.description:
BISO PLASTIQUE is an organization of people involved in the field of plastic recycling and environmental sanitation in Kinshasa, is coordinated by MOUHAMAD TSHIMBALANGA since November 2019. We are working with a group of young people to have an active, independent youth with a positive future. Biso Plastic Recycling's main focus is on the different rivers of the city of Kinshasa. We're running a workspace in Kinshasa with a shredder and an Ofen and are making a small production of goods.
We're collaborating with Oyo Projects, an NGO that reinforces informal learning in a critical approach to the aid sector in developing countries. Instead of imposing Western concepts and solutions, the project wants to create a space for experimentation and exchange to explore new strategies: How to connect local means with international concepts by deconstructing the post-colonial power structures. Oyo Projects is an association of artists, activists and other committed people. They share the wish to support street kids and young adults by engaging them in artistic and creative activities. Since 2012 the Oyo.Project team is working with street children in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

I have a lot of good ideas that could change the future by making the world a better place. Carbon Credit changes in Seattle could provide the momentum needed for a Plastic RRRevolution. I would like to see Seattle be the center of a circular plastic econonomy for the West Coast & Pacific Northwest including Alaska, Brittish Columbia, Canada and as far north as the Artic North Pole. Imagine a not to distant future where Seattle leads the way in cleaning up the ocean "Garbage Continent" in the Pacific Ocean.

Currently Seattle, Washington State, United States of America and the World at large are not doing a good job of handling plastic and other pollution. Trillions of dollars of value gets thrown away each year. Science and technology is at the propitious of a change, hopefully for the better. 

Looking for like minded people around the University of Washington that would like to explore setting up a cash positive non-profit that could explore ways to show individuals and companies best practices. Also want to leverage influence on local municipalities in Seattle Metro area and State of Washington in Olympia to use carbon tax to the benefit of the people for the people of past, current, and future. BOPE (Bope) is a brand of product made from plastic waste that has been upcycled by Khun Bo - Pemika Sutika and Khun Tue - Suparerk Tarasri, a couple who started out with their own problems. Until they saw the problems of the environment 
"We started our business buying and selling antiques. But because we didn't study well and couldn't compete with the big players, we discovered that the plastic waste was contaminated. making it impossible to import into the industry There are many outstanding items that can't be used. So I thought I'd like to use it to create value for myself. Using knowledge and skills

We have both.

The brand name BOPE (Bope) comes from the name Mr Bo, who has the same name, so his friends call him by his nickname followed by his real name (Pemika). is a rollercoaster With the idea that Chiang Mai is a tourist city. So I thought of making products that tourists could easily buy and take home, small in size and cheap.  

They started selling on Chiang Mai Walking Street. For foreigners, Upcycle products are easy to understand and popular, while for Thai people they are still new.

Thai people are still new. In the beginning, time should be spent telling the story of the piece to be understood first.

detail.name: boston-roofing
detail.shortDescription:
Boston Roofing is a family owned commercial roofing company looking to address the plastic waste issue in both the roofing and construction industry. As a roofing contractor we are given roofing materials (specifically roofing fasteners) by our materials suppliers in HDPE pails.

Firestone, Johns Manville, Carlisle and Sarnafil (the 4 major roofing materials suppliers) take no initiative or responsibility when it comes to disposing of these HDPE pails (or any of their waste for that matter). Over the course of many roofing projects, hundred of these pails are accumulated. As a roofing contractor we attempt to re-use many of these pails, but most of them end up in the DUMPSTER as the construction industry does not prioritize recycling.

Looking to gather ideas and a plan of action to address these issues through this community. Also looking to develop a work space in the next coming months, most likely starting with collection of HDPE/ sorting and shredding.

Love to hear from anyone interested in these issues as well as people who would like to get involved!!!!

Vice President -Victoria Bryan

data.description:
Established in 2014, Breckenridge Creative Arts (BCA)—or BreckCreate for short—was developed by the Town of Breckenridge to support and promote arts, culture and creative experiences throughout Breckenridge. This multidisciplinary nonprofit organization is responsible for the successful management of a series of programs, properties and partnerships that collectively animate and populate a cultural corridor in the heart of downtown Breckenridge. From quality performing and visual arts to the development of one of the region’s newest arts districts, Breckenridge Creative Arts is a transformative force for Breckenridge and the greater Summit County community.

At BreckCreate, our participation in the Precious Plastic initiative will take the form of a “Mix Workspace”, where community members and visitors to Breckenridge can transform plastic waste into art. 

In this workspace on our Arts District Campus, our team will collect clean, label-free #1, #2, #5, and #6 plastics from local businesses and community members. The plastic will then be shredded and sorted for use in BCA classes and workshops, where patrons can learn how to create new objects from plastic waste using Precious Plastic equipment. We will also offer open studios, during which time patrons who have already taken introductory classes can use the equipment without the guidance of an instructor.* 

*Plastic collection events will be held throughout Summer 2022, with classes and workshops slated to open to the public in 2023.
data.title: Precious Plastic at BreckCreate

data.description:
The Catfarm is a thriving society where everyone can learn, grow and share skills an organised community shaped by Holacracy.
In January 2021, we launched "Bridges for Plastic" to provide an opportunity to connect with our neighbours and improve our environment together! We hope to invite them to organize and create a system to collect and recycle plastic. We will organize workshops in schools and at local markets to present the process. Finally, we will make events to gather all the participants together and go further. Going further will mean generating a system of plastic currency where people would get plastic coins made out of what we collect, in exchange for 10 plastic bottles. Then, in exchange for the coins, one could receive services at the Catfarm: a handmade product, a dinner, a yoga class, etc.
5 persons constitute the Bridges for Plastic team, but this number varies depending on who lives in the community

We are Matt & Jonny of Brothers Make! We make video content based around recycling and sustainability for our YouTube channel. 

We also have a range of plastic moulding machines in our Bournemouth workshop where we sort, shred, inject and extrude recycled plastic. We mainly work with HDPE, PP and LDPE sourced from schools, beach cleans and our local community.

Our small team manufactures products that we sell on our website: www.brothersmake.com and we can also offer wholesale pricing on all of our products. Please get in touch if you are interested in a wholesale order. 

As well as manufacturing our own products, we are able to help bring your product ideas to life. If you have a product or component that you'd like to be made from 100%, locally sourced plastic with zero additives or colourants used then get in touch, we'd love to chat! (hello@brothersmake.com).

data.description:
Buinho is a fablab located in the small rural town of Messejana in the Alentejo (South Portugal). We built the machines (v2) in 2018 under the scope of an Erasmus project (www.preciousplastic.pt). With that project we were also able to help other organizations in Europe to build their own machine, provide free training to 40 young people, and start a Community recycling Center in our home town. 

In the Community Recycling Center of Buinho we:
1. Collect, separate, and transform plastic waste into new products for the local community;
2. We build new machines for other organizations and provide training in the use of the machines;
3. We develop new upgrades and customize machines and equipment's, while pursuing the development of new moulds for production

In 2020, and working for the United Nation Development Program, we built machines and provide training to a local community of Principe Island, in the small country of São Tomé e Principe. And in 2021 we aim to implement a network of Precious Plastic spaces within a wider area, empowering other neighboring communities to work with our Recycling Center.

We are the oldest Precious Plastic community center in Alentejo, covering a region that is a third of the total area of Portugal. For more information visit us @ www.buinho.pt, or contact us to info@buinho.pt
data.title: Buinho

data.description: Here at Burton ReRun the four R's have been our obsession for a while. Reduce Reuse Repair and Recycle. We think that it is about time we got serious sorting out the giant mess the planet is becoming and started building communities that are better connected, capable and resilient. We think waste is, well... wasted. It only becomes waste when you decide to throw it away! If you live in the uk you pay to have your "waste" removed, you could fill that bin with fine jewels and gold to be recycled and still be charged despite the huge value of your discarded resources. Plastics are no different, and by collecting as a community our resources are multiplied. We will use this unlocked potential to fund our community workshop and enable the community to live more sustainably, with repair cafes, access to tools and workspace, educational materials, skill sharing, social events and so much more. We want to open our doors to the community and invite everyone.  ​

data.description:
By Human is our movement to give a second life to the plastic so that it is not only thrown away, plastic was created by humans and used by humans to help humans in their activities. But sometimes many people are not aware and wise in using plastic packaging so that is it only becomes a disposable item which then becomes garbage that pollutes the environment. Through By Human, we want to show that plastic can be a functional product that has a sale value and makes people aware that humans can become heroes for the earth.


Every By Human product comes from plastic waste and natural materials such as wood and bamboo waste, therefore it can be categorized as an eco friendly product. We want to create an ethically fashion line and become a sustainable fashion brand that fully empowers local craftsmen and raw materials. Our goal is not just to sell a product, but also to become a movement that cares about the environment.

Our team is made up of people associated with the Kurka Wodna Association from Katowice, who work in the area of environmental protection, enthusiasts of the Precious Plastic movement, who have combined their competencies, skills, and passions to achieve common goals.

Our mission is to raise awareness and spread knowledge about the benefits of recycling at the individual, social, and business levels. This is based on direct and interesting workshop experiences that serve to change consumer attitudes and daily habits, and also to inspire the development of original projects.

In our vision, Cenny Plastik creates a network of cooperation that enables the active operation of workshops throughout the country, providing a space for the joint work of many people, organizations, institutions, and companies, and inspiring interesting and engaging local activities.

data.description:
In 2017, I built a modified shredder to shredder and recycle EVA footwear for Native Shoes in Vancouver. The idea was based around PP's shredder design, with an upgraded motor, stand, and other safety accessories like an emergency shut off.

Native Shoes has since started The Remix Project, where they collect old pairs of shoes, shred them and turn them into new materials. This material has been used as seat padding in their flagship store in Gastown (Vancouver), and is now going to be used as playground matting as well.

Read more here: https://www.nativeshoes.com/ca/blog/the-remix-project.html
And here: https://zapposforgood.org/recycle/native

data.description:
I want to use my daily life to enhance the world that surrounds me.  That is by helping with local trash pick ups, clothing swaps, and using my dollar as my vote. To reiterate the first R in Recycling, I try my best to refuse any purchase that will not have a second resource life.  By understanding the benefits of reducing individual trash, we can continue to create packaging that will not harm our environment and have a shared knowledge of the ecosystem we participate in.  

Community Point
I love Denton.  The people, the music, and the community that cherishes each other.  I want to create a place that reuses and recreates the life of plastic and I know I can help make it happen.  I work with trash every day.  I see plastic, food, and materials that can moved from the waste stream and cherished in lieu of destroyed and damaged by tossing in one big pile.  I hope to use my work place for future extrusion, collection and have a machine shop in mind for any casting and forms needed.  I am excited to collaborate, brain storm and be a functioning Precious Plastic Denton.   I will reach out to our outlets including Keep Denton Beautiful, Don't Dump on Denton, and Better Understating of Trash Through Service.  

Description
Write a little text about your group and activities. Every Sunday 7pm North Lakes Disc Golf Clean up. Meet up, play disc golf and pick up trash along the way. 
- When did you start? - 7/15/2020
- How big is your group? 3 people

- Do you have regular meetup times or open days? And when? Sundays at 7pm North Lakes Park

detail.displayName: Central Institute Of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET), Korba

data.description:
A unit of CIPET has been established in the city of Korba situated at Power City of Chhattisgarh, in September 2018 with the joint efforts of Govt. of India and Govt. of Chhattisgarh with a special focus to provide academic and employment oriented skill development training to the Unemployed/Underemployed youths of Chhattisgarh & to provide technical support service to plastics and allied industries. CIPET is located at Education Hub, Syahimudi, Post - Gopalpur, Korba. The area of campus is 18.2 acres.

By seeing the emerging need and growth of Plastics Industries in Northern part of Chhattisgarh. CIPET, Korba is going to start long term academic programme along with the skill development programme for meeting the upcoming needs and demands of the unemployed youths of Chhattisgarh in General, Scheduled Tribe, Schedule Cast and youths of the L.W.E. districts in particular and enhance their technical skills & providing them Self Wage employment for bringing them to the main stream.

CIPET, Korba will be providing training and technical consultancy services in the field of Design, CAD/CAM/CAE, Tool Room, Plastic Processing and Testing. The centre has following specific objective in various areas of training, technical and research & development activities. The centre is consistently processing in terms of training and technical services.

OBJECTIVES :
To generate technical manpower through various academic programmes for plastics processing and allied industries in and around Chhattisgarh.
To develop technicaly skilled manpower for the need of plastics & allied industries in India and abroad through various short-term training programmes.
To conduct short-term programmes for updating the technical knowledge, skill and competency of the manpower in the plastic industry.
To organized Entrepreneur Development Programmes (EDP) to motivate and promote the trainees to become entrepreneurs in the field of plastics.
Quality Control and Standardization of plastic materials and Product Technical, Consultancy and Advisory Services for enhancing Techno Commercial Competitiveness.
Fabrication of Moulds, Dyes & process of Plastic Products.
data.title: Central Institute Of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET), Korba

CODE CV is a Social Development Cooperative. We defend the promotion of quality tourism, social cohesion, equal opportunities and empowerment of people and institutions. We focus on the development of collaborative learning processes and new skill sets.

Our mission is to boost Cape Verde’s sustainable development through the execution of activities in the scope of tourism; training; international projects and partnerships for development; empowerment and implementation of local people and businesses, sustainable development projects as well as social, community intervention and organisation of events.

Among other projects, we've set up a Plastic Recycling Unit where the goal is to reduce the ecological footprint created mainly by tourists but also by the locals, raising awareness for the reutilisation of plastic as a raw material, to be used for production of new items.

data.description: I am an experienced and versatile professional, with a rich and diverse career spanning more than 7 years in various areas. My career is notably marked by a consistent focus on management, leadership and innovation. My trajectory includes the application of agile methodologies, such as Scrum, Kanban, Lean and the creation of Software and Hardware Products, complemented by the use of collaboration tools such as Git, Jira, Confluence, Monday, Notion, Miro, Canva and Pipedrive. These skills have been crucial in facilitating the efficient management of creative, technical and commercial teams. Additionally, I am proficient in implementing strategic techniques, including OKR for goal setting and measurement, as well as SWOT and PESTAL analyzes to map secondary data and assess business opportunities, threats, strengths, and weaknesses. As a portfolio manager, I led the strategic management of projects and resources, including financial analysis, fundraising and coordination of complex projects with the aim of analyzing risks of a portfolio of environmental assets, including carbon projects. This experience demonstrates my ability to make strategic decisions and lead multidisciplinary initiatives to achieve effective results in a challenging business environment. In previous roles as Product Manager, I led technology teams on challenging projects, focusing on innovation and the development of high-performance products. My experience in aerospace engineering and free technology organizations broadens my knowledge in multidisciplinary leadership and complex problem solving. My most recent experience as a Continental Coordinator has allowed me to lead regional and continental strategies, as well as conduct research into regenerative systems. My passion for innovation and sustainable development is evident in my contributions to cutting-edge theory such as Hyperautonomy and Modular Eco Industries, as well as an ongoing commitment to adopting best management practices.

data.description:
Hi, my name is Donald Martin García Gonzalez and I live at the beautiful Lake Atitlán in Guatemala. After living in Japan with my family for 13 years, we came back to Guatemala where I bought land at the lake - but: It was full of plastic garbage. 

My 5-year-old son had a talk with the insects in our land and they said: "Please, tell your dad: We cannot live in plastic. Please do something!" This made me think.

And I asked God, what to do. What he said was: "Build an oven!" I am a crazy artist, not an ingeneer. But I tried and tried and finally, I built an oven. But the final design came from God again, so I built another oven which melts plastic. And this one really works. It has the shape of one pyramide flipped on another one and runs on fire through burning paper - no electricity, no gasoline.

So what I want to do now is to clean the lake first and then melt the plastics into blocks in order to reuse our waste. But I'm at the very beginning, and I've spent all my money already. That's why I am happy to be part of this wonderful community - so please get in touch if you'd like to support me!
data.title: derretidor de plastico

data.description:
We (Maxwell and Adam) are recently graduated 4th year business students from St. Francis Xavier University (St.FX) in Nova Scotia, Canada. As a team, we are passionate about environmental sustainability and plastic waste reduction and we believe that radical changes are necessary to address the plastic waste crisis we all face. 

It is our mission to expand on the work of Precious Plastic, by introducing a fully sustainable recycling program on the St.FX University campus. We will be building the Precious Plastic shredder, extrusion, and injection machines locally, gathering post-consumed plastic from St.FX students, and selling repurposed plastic products on campus. Additionally, we will be hosting educational workshops designed to empower students.

data.description: Ecomonte es una cooperativa de carácter de triple impacto, ya que nuestro compromiso no es solo generar efectos positivos en el medio ambiente. si no también en la sociedad de consumo y la economía regional.   Somos jóvenes involucrados con el medio ambiente y nos preocupa el futuro de nuestro planeta, es por eso que al reciclar y reutilizar residuos plásticos y transformarlos en materia prima de calidad, contribuimos a la reducción de la contaminación a cielo abierto y a la reducción de tala de arboles nativos.   Además nos preocupa nuestra comunidad, es por eso que colaboramos con organizaciones locales de recolectores para fomentar el desarrollo productivo y la sostenibilidad de la región. Asimismo, nos interesa educar y concientizar a las actuales y futuras generaciones sobre la importancia de cuidar el medio ambiente, reducir la huella de carbono y dejar un mundo mejor al que nos encontramos.   Nos divierte mucho poner manos a la obra e involucrarnos en el desarrollo tecno-productivo, es por eso que estamos constantemente en la busqueda de soluciones innovadoras que generen un impacto ambiental positivo, y a la vez ofrecer un producto de calidad, agradable y duradero para nuestros clientes.  Estamos muy contentos de formar parte de este movimiento hacia un mundo más sostenible y consciente, pero solos no podemos, por eso te invitamos a unirte a colaborar con nosotros y dejar de ser parte del problema para formar parte de la solución.

data.description:
The Ecopazífico Foundation designed, formulated, and donated to the Community Council of the Black Community of Juanchaco, a Recycling Center for the treatment of recyclable material consistent with the social and territorial conditions of coastal and remote populations lacking infrastructure for waste management.

The Recycling Center operates with solar panels and a cistern system that works from rainwater, thanks to the support of the organization Givepower. The black communities of Bahía Málaga can now document, wash, shred, and initially transform four different types of rigid plastic using medium-scale machines inspired from Precious Plastic models and will eventually be able to treat glass, styrofoam, flip-flops, and light plastic, which are abundant in the territory and constitute an environmental and sanitary threat to its inhabitants and ecosystems. 

With the hard work and support of the communities of Bahía Málaga, international environmental organizations, national and foreign companies, hundreds of volunteers, universities, private donors, and public entities, we are contributing to the conservation of a territory that is a humpback whales’ sanctuary, home to more than 3,600 species of animals, as well as contributing to the resilience of coastal communities facing climate change, fostering circular economy and sustainable tourism.

Thank you for supporting us!
data.title: Ecopazifico Foundation

data.description:
Welcome to Fiji EcoPlast Recyclers!

At Fiji EcoPlast Recyclers, we're dedicated to making a positive impact on our beautiful island environment. As pioneers in sustainable plastic recycling solutions, we're committed to transforming plastic waste into valuable resources. Our mission is to reduce the ecological footprint of plastic pollution while contributing to a greener and cleaner Fiji.

What Sets Us Apart:

🌱 Environmental Stewardship: We're driven by a passion for preserving Fiji's natural beauty. Our state-of-the-art recycling technology allows us to process plastic waste responsibly and efficiently.

♻️ Circular Economy Champions: Embracing the principles of a circular economy, we breathe new life into discarded plastics, preventing them from ending up in our oceans and landscapes.

🌊 Ocean Guardians: Situated in the heart of the Pacific, we're committed to safeguarding our oceans. Through innovative recycling techniques, we're part of the solution to marine plastic pollution.

🌏 Community Collaboration: We believe that creating a sustainable future requires collaboration. We work closely with local communities, businesses, and governments to foster awareness and sustainable practices.

Our Services:

data.description:
Envirohub Bay of Plenty is the hub organisation for more than 15 projects across the Bay, partnering with local and regional councils as well as a range of community groups and partners. We provide support for sustainable choices and positive action to help the environment. 

Envirohub exists to provide a point of connection between individuals, groups, organisations, and local and central government agencies that are acting to create change, regeneration and growth within our natural and urban environments. Our mission is to provide our community access to a vast network of educators, creatives, and funders that are providing solutions to natural and urban environmental challenges we are living with today. To create a living library of knowledge through provide multi-platform access to contributors to the environmental network in the Bay of Plenty.

data.description:
I'm Esau from Japan. I made Shredder, Injection, Extrusion by myself and trying to bring these machines and create Precious plastic community in to Kosrae island, Federated States of Micronesia which is the most beautiful island in the world.
Why Micronesia?  I used to be working in Kosrae Island resource management authority and saw a bunch of plastic wastes piling up on this beautiful island because of imported products or plastic wastes which arrived from overseas like my country, Japan. That made me so sad and thought that I want to do something for this island and protect the beautiful nature. 
Right now, I'm working on Precious Plastic in Japan because of Coronavirus. But I'll be back when this pandemic is over.

That experience showed us that it was possible to promote a digital manufacturing space and also to convince the administration of this opportunity. Over the last few months we have been working in order to develop a slowly-growing maker space.

We want to become a community point to gather and develop ideas for the commons. We are building the Shredder, the Injection and the Biopress. Besides that, we will have other machines that you can work with and run workshops.

data.description: This is a low-tech plastic recycling workspace. I explore and experiment with recycling techniques that are accessible to everyone and that anyone can replicate at home with minimal tools.  Not being able to shred plastic is a limitation, but it is also exciting to discover what you can achieve without it and find which plastic product is suitable for this process.  The production is based on the compression technique (oven + cold press) and the outcome is mostly focused on artworks, product design and plastic sheets (45x35 cm) production.

data.description: Soy Federico Olthoff CEO de fabricadesoluciones3d-Brindamos el servicio de diseño digital y manufactura. Traslade mi empresa a un pueblo de pie de montaña con 1300 habitantes,de los cuales solo 870+- radican de manera permanente. El colegio cuenta con 103 alumnos, entre ellos en nivel primario,secundario y adultos mayores. La inserción laboral es escasa y la migración a las ciudad es cada vez mas escasa por la economía del lugar. Como diseñador Industrial y habitante del pueblo, tras ver la problemática me propuse intervenir. Actualmente brindamos un taller en conjunto con el municipio sobre nuevas tecnologías,la economía del conocimiento y el valor agregado para potenciar las economías regionales, pero sobre todo mostrarle a los jóvenes la posibilidad de algo distinto. A esto le sumamos el desafió de generar una planta de reciclado que produzca valor y fuentes de trabajo a nuestros habitantes. transformando el plástico que contamina nuestro hermoso paisaje, en artilugios y objetos.
data.title: fabricadesoluciones3d

data.description:
Qui sommes-nous?

Pratico Plastique est une coopérative qui s'engage dans la lutte aux changements climatiques en proposant une solution aux enjeux de l'impact environnemental des déchets plastiques.

Notre mission

Être le partenaire #1 de sensibilisation et de revalorisation des déchets plastiques auprès des entreprises et de la population Québécoise; possible grâce à notre offre de service de transformation des déchets en mobilier utiles recyclés. De plus, nous nous
engageons socialement dans la création d'emplois équitables à travers la région. Nous souhaitons contribuer au rayonnement de la province québécoise en termes de solutions écoresponsables face à une problématique universelle.

Comment?

Nous nous appuyons sur une approche à circuit court pour l’accès à nos services et l'instauration de la gestion complète de la matière plastique de la collecte jusqu'à la transformation en produits durables. De plus, nous nous engageons socialement dans la
création d'emplois équitables à travers la région et le rayonnement de la province québécoise en termes de solutions écoresponsables à une grave problématique universelle.
data.title: Pratico Plastique

Born in february 2021, this fablab is close to 4 schools (2600 kids) in a small and cosy place called "Domaine de Labourdonnais". Perfect place for this fablab with the goal to sensitise, train and present another point of view on plastic waste. For 2023 we have had more than 2000 visitors (in the Fablab or to other places). We have one full time ambassador (and had 4 volunteers). With his Cargobike he goes from school to school (and other places to sensitize, collect and present Freedom Plastic). During the year we also had a collaboration with Jon (artisan) who produced awesome awards based on our plastic production. This year we also have started a new program called Mauritius Plastic Challenge www.mauritiusplastic.com a national commitment of Mauritius against plastic pollution. Please join us for a visit or a partnership Call Greg at +230 54 22 53 54 or plastic at missionverte.com

data.description:
Our Community Recycling Lab was born in a workshop with rural youth where we had to present a solution to a problem we cared about. In our small rural town we do not have an adequate waste management system. Only 48% of waste even gets collected. The rest in burnt or thrown in rivers and creekbeds. In order to tackle these problems, we decided to take waste management into our own hands. Eight students started the lab. We began by building the shredder and extrusion machines. After experimenting with the different plastics with decided to focus on working with HDPE. Currently we are producing plastic rods which we are selling to the local floriculture businesses. They use these to hold the flower beds. They were using wooden sticks. but these rot and they have to buy new sticks each flower cycle. By replacing them with plastic rods they are using less wood and can reuse the rods year after year. 
It is very important to note that for us education is at the core of our project. We work with students and the community as a whole to create consciousness and awareness of our pollution. We have given several workshops about the dangers of burning plastics and the importance of recycling and have designed a community recollection system in two communities. Additionally, we are also fronting another problem: the lack of opportunities for rural youth. Through our lab, young people can explore the world of investigation, learn and design projects, and create an innovative micro-enterprise.Our project is driven by the community’s youth. The community designed the project, runs the lab and benefits from the results.
Our Lab is hosted in FUCAE a local NGO that focuses on environment and education. They were able to help us with the seed capital to get started.

In 2022, this home business of ours has really started flow! We've created a new workspace in a converted camper-trailer parked in our driveway. We have a V4 shredder, injector, & extruder made by Citizen Scientific Workshop. 

We aim to further the Precious Plastic cause by demonstrating how small scale, eco-friendly recycling could operate independently anywhere on the planet.

data.description:
A poluição do ambiente através de plásticos é um fenómeno que ocorre a uma velocidade estonteante, um problema que atravessa todos os países ao qual não podemos escapar por isso é impossível ficarmos indiferentes, uma vez que a nossa saúde depende do ambiente que nos rodeia e porque mundo só há um, logo há que cuidar dele, e o meio ambiente é a pedra basilar para a qualidade de vida dos seres vivos bem como para a sua sustentabilidade. E sendo este um problema à escala global, mas defendemos e acreditamos que as soluções devem ser locais. Mediante este flagelo, a nossa Associação de Pais e Encarregados de Educação do Agrupamento de Escolas de Vila Pouca de Aguiar (APEEVPA), que trabalha com os alunos e para os alunos e em prol do seu bem-estar , jamais poderia adotar uma postura passiva ou ͞fechar os olhos͟ a este problema que é de todos nós, mas sim um papel proativo na proteção e defesa do nosso meio ambiente, pois a preservação dos vários ecossistemas é um fator de preocupação, por isso cada vez mais é necessário e urgente o envolvimento da nossa comunidade educativa na preservação dos ecossistemas, elementos fundamentais para o bem-estar. E acima de tudo é urgente olharmos para as nossas crianças de hoje e pensar nelas como os nossos adultos de amanhã. Assim, torna-se indispensável consciencializá-las para os problemas ambientais, a fim de que adotem medidas no sentido de os colmatar/ solucionar e transmitir isso às gerações vindouras. data.description: I was born in Bairnsdale, Victoria, Australia on Gunaikurnai Country. I am proud to be a descendant of the Yuin Mob from the Southeast Coast of NSW.  Driven by my passion for the environment and a strong desire to contribute to its protection, I embarked on my first personal business venture.  Gardening on Country was established in 2023 with a mission to foster a circular economy, where the utilisation of recycled plastic products becomes the standard.  It was during a family photography session at the beach that I noticed and was concerned about all of the rubbish and plastic that surrounded us as we posed. Looking at the rubbish strewn around my family got me thinking, how could we utilise this forgotten rubbish? Was there another way to divert it from landfill and our waterways to give it another purpose?  So began the rabbit hole of research into recycled plastic, circular economies and repurposing that led to the creation of Gardening on Country!   All of our tools are hand made in Australia from recycled plastic lids that are shredded down and then melted before being extruded into a mould.  The plastic lids are made from high density poly ethylene (HDPE 2) and are commonly found on water or soft drink bottles.   We are dedicated to delivering top-notch, long-lasting tools that are user-friendly and require minimal upkeep.
data.title: GardeningonCountry

data.description:
sobre nós
O Projeto Mar Sem Lixo atua desde 2010 na Região dos Lagos, Costa do Sol e Baía de Guanabara, um trabalho
de conscientização e educação ambiental, identificação e controle do lixo marinho por meio de mutirões de
limpeza de praias, pesquisas, palestras e execução de projetos relacionados.
Sempre em parceria com a comunidade local, escolas, associações esportivas, prefeituras, instituições privadas,
Colônia de Pescadores, instituições públicas e ambientais como o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) e o Instituto
Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio), Colônias de Pescadores e população em geral.
As principais ações do Projeto Mar Sem Lixo se materializam por meio de projetos e campanhas de mobilização
social, comunicação visual e mídias sociais, monitoramento, pesquisa da poluição e limpeza das praias, defesa
dos recursos hídricos e educação ambiental. A nossa preocupação está também relacionada com a
sustentabilidade das populações que dependem dos recursos existentes nas zonas costeiras, pois atuamos para
prevenir e remover os plásticos que entram nos nossos oceanos e impactam o meio marinho. Nesse sentido,
ressaltamos a importância da implantação de projetos de gestão de resíduos, principalmente nas cidades
litorâneas, beneficiando assim cooperativas e recicladores, que geralmente vivem à margem da sociedade,
aliviando assim o descarte incorreto e o impacto desses resíduos nos ecossistemas. População ribeirinha e
colônias de pesca.
data.title: Projeto Mar Sem Lixo

data.description: GudRnD is a group of engineers in the Gudskul Ecosystem. This group was initiated by Studio Bagendit aka studio batur Jakarta branch with Gudskul. This group aims to provide alternative knowledge by experimenting and engineering. This group likes to do experiments including indoor hydroponics experiments, electronics experiments, mechanics experiments and plastic packaging recycling experiments. Currently, GudRnD is focusing on recycling several types of plastics to make daily products with an exchange transaction system with plastic packaging. GudRnD is open to collaborating and sharing experiences in trying as one of the distribution of knowledge.

Hello ! 

J'ai pris connaissance du projet Precious Plastic en 2016, sans vraiment sauter le pas ! 

Aujourd'hui j'ai envie de passer à une autre étape qui serait de mettre en place un workspace dans l'un de mes pays d'origines : les Comores (Grande-Comores plus précisément).

Pour l'instant ne sachant pas trop par ou commencer, je collecte les informations utiles et participe un peu plus au sein de la communauté. 

See you

data.description: Helpertunity is an inclusionary enterprise charity; serving the social-learning and voluntainment needs of elderly, disabled, and itinerant makers - with a focus on the arts, upcycling, technology, and vintage gameplay. The charity was founded by two former schoolteachers in 2010; located in central Florida, USA.  Our efforts in 2021 and beyond include designing handicap-accessible methods and activities that make helping the planet more fun!  We have been clipping (and will soon be shredding) the least-recyclable varieties of single-use plastics to create colorful EcoBricks.  Our plastic-packed bottle-shaped bricks will be used for building decorative playhouses and puppet-scapes, and for making Expo Booth Decor for use at our Eco-Carnival Game & Craft Activities Outreach & Fundraiser Days.  Our games include a Wishing-Well bottlecap pitch, and a Ring-A-BottleBrick toss, among others; where donors win pre-loved-plush prizes for their contributions and participation.  Our crafts activities include packing colorful 'Bottled (P)sand Art' granules and flakes using safe and handicap-assistive bottle-packing devices.  We provide our Eco-Carnival activities at local Youth and Elder Maker-Outreach days, and while visiting select Eldercare Facilities and Senior Communities to provide recreation, entertainment, and gentle fitness interactions.
data.title: Helpertunity's Eco-Carnival

During the jurassic period (180 Mio years ago) -  when Ichtyosauruses were alive - plankton fell as a sediment onto the sea ground. It later became mineral oil - the basic of plastic production. Like PET bottles. I collect wasted PET bottles at the seaside, shredder them, make filament out of it to print a 6 m long Ichtyosaur... The circle is closed!

data.description:
IN MOCEAN is a not for profit organisation based in Germany that helps communities in remote coastal areas to set up small-scale plastic recycling workspaces. The aim is to keep plastic out of nature and create an incentive to remove it from nature at the same time. In cooperation with a suitable local organisation, we set up the infrastruture for decentralized recycling that has a positive impact for the local population on three levels: economical, ecological and social.

We have a fleet of sailing recycling ambassadors that visit remote communities to create awareness about the potential of small-sacle recycling. With the help of mobile recycling machines, they show the transformation from trash to treasure and provide information on how to set up a recycling workspace.

You live in a remote coastal community and would like to set up a small-scale recycling workspace? We would love to hear from you and try to help where we can.

Thanks for being #inmoceanforcleanoceans
data.title: IN MOCEAN

data.description: Instauro Renewables is a company focused on reducing the amount of plastic waste that ends up in our environment. Instauro produces consumer products and commercial plastic pellets from single use plastic that was bound for landfills. The goal is to lead the charge against pollution and push each individual to live a more sustainable lifestyle.   Instauro Renewables is committed to making sure each product we create is made from recycled plastic. In addition to this, we ensure that all of our packaging is recyclable so no excess waste is created in our distribution process.    Instauro Renewables dreams of the day we can walk down the street without seeing garbage scattered along the side that will take thousands of years to degrade. Each step we take is in pursuit of this mission and in hopes of a cleaner environment for us to live our everyday lives.

data.description:
"We are an organization dedicated to the transformation and redefinition of Brasília's city center through community engagement and the activation of public spaces with culture, art, and creative economy. Since our inception as a cultural collective in early 2018, we have played a crucial role in the quest for the revitalization of the Setor Comercial Sul (South Commercial Sector) and in fostering an integrated experience between the local community and the space. Through projects initiated by the community or our institute, we aim to strengthen the social and cultural bonds existing in the region, creating deeper connections among those who frequent the area.

We acknowledge the challenges posed by the ongoing process of gentrification in the central region and the need to make efforts to ensure that the area remains open to the public, free, and welcoming to the groups already present in the region. We believe that the heart of Brasília has the potential to develop activities in the creative economy, involving thousands of people who work in or enjoy culture, leisure, gatherings, and communal spaces. In 2022, the sectors comprising the Creative Economy generated R$ 9 billion in the Federal District (2nd Creative Economy Overview Report), and the city center is an integral part of this dynamic."

data.description:
The Catfarm is an off-grid community of travelers, (digital) nomads, artists, healers, entrepreneurs, and purpose-driven people with the will to explore an alternative lifestyle closer to nature.
In January 2021, we launched "Bridges for Plastic" to provide an opportunity to connect with our neighbours and improve our environment together! We hope to invite them to organize and create a system to collect and recyce plastic. We will organıze workshops in schools and at local markets to present the process. Finally, we will make events to gather all the participants together and go further. Going further will mean generating a system of plastic currency where people would get plastic coins made out of what we collect, in exchange for 10 plastic bottles. Then, in exchange for the coins, one could receive services at the Catfarm: a handmade product, a dinner, a yoga class, etc.
5 persons constıtute the Brıdges for Plastıc team, but thıs number varıes dependıng on who lıves ın the communıty.

data.description: My name is Ivaenia De Giacomi, people call me Iva. I am from Paraguay, I work as a civil engineer in the infrastructure construction field. Since I began my professional career, residues caused by leftover construction materials have always been a concern as a person in charge. In my country there is no policy for recycling materials in general, there are small companies that do it as a business and as a way to earn a living, however, I see an urgent need to analyze alternatives related to the construction sector. Not only as a professional but as a citizen of my beloved country, I would like to start this project that seemed fascinating to me from the first minute I saw it in "one army" regarding the recycling of plastics.

data.description:
Plastiz is an Italian startup created in response to the environmental and social emergencies caused by the growing invasion of plastic waste. It is a concrete contribution to circular economic processes where plastic waste is reused for the production of high quality surfaces and semi-finished products.

We strongly believe in education. We want to contribute to the adoption of responsible behaviors, promoting a change of perception towards plastic, from disposable to durable good. We organize workshops, webinars and trainings for schools, companies and institutions, promoting an ethics of responsibility and providing tools for a conscious management of plastic waste.

As part of the Precious Plastic Universe we make our Makerspace available to rent for the production of 40 x 40 centimeters panels. Users can contribute to the project, grind their own plastic material, and thermoform it for their creations.

Hello, I am Jarvis a Data scientist living in Japan. I am a Nomad worker using a service called ADDress. I set up a trash collection group in the ADDress community and now looking to start recycling while on the move. The first step is to set up a mobile workstation inside a van, then a physical business (recycling cafe), run as an NPO to support the development of trash management and recycling in Nepal. If your interest in the project contact me on Instagram 
(Japanese bellow)

ジャービス(仁)と申します。ADDressというサービスを使用して、日本で働きながら旅しています。
ADDressのコミュニケーションの中で社会人のゴミ回収部（部長になった(笑)）を設立しました。次の一歩は、リサイクリングです。今の計画では、最初に軽バンでリサイクリングのワークスパースを作りたいです。
ここで、イベントやゴミ回収を行いながら、リサイクリングできます。次の一歩は、起業です。
リサイクリングのカフェのコンセプトというコンセントは、お客様はプラステックを寄付すれば、無料コーヒーを与えるものです。そして、このビジネスはNPO法人で、利益はネパールでリサイクリングや清掃活動を応援するために使いたいです。興味がある方は自由に連絡ください
現在のビジネスプランはこのシートの中です。

Before discovering Precious Plastic, I embarked on a personal initiative to recycle plastic into interlocks, making a significant impact as the pioneer of this endeavor in Nigeria. Although the process was manual, it laid a solid foundation for my understanding of plastic recycling techniques and their potential for environmental sustainability. This experience ignited a deep fascination within me for exploring innovative approaches to plastic recycling and finding ways to create a positive change in my community.

As a member of the Precious Plastic community, I hope to leverage my academic background in chemistry to contribute valuable insights and technical knowledge to ongoing projects. My understanding of the chemical properties of plastics, as well as my expertise in identifying different types of plastics, can be instrumental in developing efficient recycling methods and exploring new avenues for plastic repurposing.

Moreover, I bring a strong sense of dedication, perseverance, and problem-solving skills to the table. My experience in working with limited resources has honed my ability to find creative solutions and adapt to various challenges. I am eager to collaborate with like-minded individuals who share a common goal of mitigating plastic pollution and creating a more sustainable future.

Through my involvement in the Precious Plastic community, I hope to connect with individuals who are passionate about plastic recycling and engage in meaningful discussions, exchange knowledge, and collaborate on impactful projects. I am open to learning from the expertise of others and expanding my own horizons within the realm of plastic recycling

Being an island we have to pay to transport materials off the island to mainland collection centres, which eats into an already low profit margin. data.description: Violet has been interested in this project since inception, and moved to Chicago with the intention of creating a fully functional workshop in the city. Violet is very passionate about recycling, utilizing reusable materials, and beautifying the world around us. She’s and avid networker, and is capable of creating events to get more local community members involved. 2020 was a wild time for all of us, and plans for a trailer and machines for plastic were put on hold. Violet has built a small propane foundry for melting aluminum cans. Plans to connect the community so we can create a loop of materials is the plan for 2021 and beyond! 2023 update: have been spending some time with the fine folk at Redemptive Plastics in the Austin neighborhood. Violet is also utilizing scrap fabrics into new textiles.

data.description:
Headquartered in Port-au-Prince, FdS works on all fronts to stop Haiti’s deforestation and the devastating effects of Haiti's dependence on charcoal. We also work to improve the health and lives of cooks, educate the public on safe cooking practices, and find solutions to Haiti’s abysmal management of its waste materials.

We collect post-consumer waste material from institutions around Port-au-Prince and find as many local recycling solutions as we can.
FdS Haiti is the exclusive UN contractor for recyclables in the Port-au-Prince region, including plastic, paper, cardboard, and aluminum. 
We recycle waste paper, cardboard, and sawdust into clean-burning briquette fuel blocks to replace charcoal cooking, with accompanying efficient stoves.
We are currently working to implement the PreciousPlastic model in Haiti with the importation of examples of all types of PreciousPlastic processing machines, which we subsequently hope to duplicate in Haiti. 

We work to divert as much material as possible away from Haiti’s blighted regional dumps. It is our mission to give materials a second life through our innovative recycling processes.



Our office is located at: 

#8 Rue St Fleure 
Tabarre 23, Port-Au-Prince, Haiti
data.title: FdS Haiti/ Fuego del Sol Haiti

data.description:
I am a driller by trade.  I have designed and implemented a successful, light weight hydraulic drill.


I was asked by our local recycling depot to complete a Precious Plastic shredder, and possible extruder.

Having trouble sourcing 110V, gear driven, electric motors, I put together a 3hp electric over hydraulic system.

We are in the middle of trying to bring this project to a close.  We might move to a gas powered shredder to determine horsepower requirements.


I am looking to offer the specifications of our design, and the problems encountered, to help expand the Precious Plastic community knowledge base.

I am looking forward to sharing information and ideas.

Here is a link to a YouTube video of our shredder:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQmSl18iMWU

All the best to all involved,

-Sean Payne, Dawson City, Yukon
data.title: kingopayne

data.description: We are a collaboration between the Non-profit Association Gaia Protection and the Bamberger Lebenshilfe. It's a parent association who aims to offer adapted jobs for people with all kind of disabilities and train them to eventually enter the labour market. We installed a recycling workplace at the Lebenshilfe, so the persons who work there would have a meaningful and sustainable work. We own a shredder and a injector to produce small goods. The produced objects are sold and the money is being reinvested in the workplace and the NGO Gaia Protection. Meanwhile Gaia Protection organizes interacitve workshops with the machines in schools and festival to raise awareness for plastic pollution, innovative solutions and hopefully engage people for behavioral change! We set up collection points in schools and in the residential groups of the Lebenshilfe for now. We soon hope to expand the collection points to other places in our beloved hometown Bamberg!

My name is Harold Sokyrka, and I am an innovator from Saskatoon Canada, I have developed a Patent Pending Licensed System that will significantly improve the collection of the quality & quantity of household recycling materials BEFORE they enter the waste and recycling stream. My company has been operating for over 3 years and we focus on Eco-friendly products for the householder and commercial businesses.

I am pleased to announce that we have a joint venture partner in the USA, and we will be expanding our products and “System” into the US market later this year.


PRESS RELEASE

https://tinyurl.com/3mxf987t


Our Mission Statement give you a basic understanding of the “System”. 
https://youtu.be/z9dutZzgvPA

data.description:
The association was born in April 2014 from the meeting of utopians from Amiens who aspired to "make and work differently". By creating a digital workshop (fablab) associated with a shared work space (coworking), they wanted to experiment with a different way of making society. data.description:
Artistes pluridisciplinaires et "makers" dans l'âme, les membres de l'association Indiens dans la ville, associent leurs connaissances à travers différents procédés : travaux photographiques, affichage urbain, impression 3D, installations dans l’espace public … Poursuivant une réflexion ouverte et collaborative sur les manières de voir la ville et les différentes façons d'y agir.

C'est passionné par les nouvelles technologies, à l'heure où la fabrication numérique et les projets opensource se démocratisent, que l'association IDLV souhaite être acteur du changement visant à favoriser une manière logique et humaniste de vivre en cohérence avec l’environnement dans le contexte urbain d'aujourd’hui.
