data.description:
Les Petits Labos is an interdisciplinary research and creation laboratory. Its main objective is to explore new modes of eco-responsible production in the service of artistic creation. Based at Coco Velten in Marseille, this laboratory, led by Diego Ortiz and Hernan Zambrano, promotes a convergence between art, ecology and new technologies.
With the aim of designing projects capable of tackling the complexity of the environmental challenge in an innovative way, they are now experimenting with different kinds of biomaterials. Their research leads them to use, for example, the data captured by air quality monitoring agencies, to transform them, through digital programming, into innovative objects composed of light, movement and sound. .
They are also interested in the development of plastic waste transformation processes for the benefit of alternative artistic production.
Diego Ortiz and Hernan Zambrano strive to combine aesthetic issues, functional and productive qualities, with a renewed and more responsible vision of art. An art born from a true economy in the treatment of natural resources before, during and after the creation of a work.
data.title: Les Petits Labos

data.description:
Precious Plastic ACT is a partnership between Lids4Kids Australia, Rethink Recycling Co-op and Precious Plastic.

Lids4Kids Australia is a grass-roots 100% volunteer project which rescues plastic bottle lids from landfill to benefit the environment. Our volunteers wash and dry the lids, then sort them by colour and polymer. We then granulate the lids so that they can be extruded into molds to create sustainable recycled plastic products.

Here in the ACT, we are helping to set up four workshops:
1) PlasLink ACT
2) Pretty Poly 
3) Aranda Primary School
4) Lids4Kids Canberra

Cheers, Tim Miller 

Founder, Lids4Kids Australia 
2020 ACT Volunteer of the Year 
2020 ACT Belconnen Westfield Local Hero
2021 ACT Local Hero
data.title: Precious Plastic ACT & Lids4Kids Australia

data.description:
Limpi recycling is a unique company that uses local plastic waste to create new products. They also create their own machines, designs and molds. The production process is done on Curacao therefore having a completely locally made product. How cool is that!

Limpi is founded by two young entrepreneurs, Debrah Nijdam and Mitchell Lammering. They make a large variety of products from small to big. They started of with making keychains and coasters and are now able to make table-tops, trash bins and much more.

They are also known for their custom-made products. Companies can contact them to make custom merchandise, awards or a product that they would like to design from scratch.
After all, Debrah and Mitchell are Product engineers and love a good challenge.

Their products stand out because they are created to make an impact. The products offer a solution for the plastic waste of Curaçao creating a circular economy. It also shows how valuable plastic waste is. Encouraging more people to recycle.

data.description:
The Plastic Waste Management at Plasmo Hub platform allows users to exchange the credit of the collected material for products for themselves, sales on the website or services.
If people choose to sell something, they earn a percentage of the final price, which will vary between short or long storage period that product takes.
The rental of Collection Stations active the Admin account, in the application, for points receiving, which this user can manage to create projects and engage other logged in users around collection areas.
The standard account allows users to gain points distributed from Admins and participate in campaigns promoted on the platform, which include voting, competitions, events and classes.
It work as a game to engage pursuit and measure solutions people create for their plastic outputs, to keep on being an input somewhere on the value chain, as any material in the world deserves.

The recycling workshop serves as a basis for the organization’s application interface and user experience, and it's interconnected to the locations of Collection Stations we strategically allocate.
The production system is based on manufacture of items we will pre-validate in the adopted technology.
Plan is to use a Plastell or some other NIR spectrography sorting, washing machine, shredder, sheetpress, saw, sandpaper,and carpentry process.
We aim at reaching in 6 months the capacity to transform 1100 to 1400 kilograms per month into products designed to last and serve much longer, having at least 30% of products made on-demand.
Our implementation program has not started out, now stage is building partnership with stakeholders for a service contract during MVP.
data.title: Plasmo hub

data.description: I've been a green advocate all my life and have been a follower of Precious Plastic ever since I saw Dave Hakkens' first YouTube videos in 2013. Since then, I've been collecting and segregating all sorts of plastics at home and from the office where I worked. Eventually, I was able to save enough and bought the V2 shredder from Precious Plastic Philippines back in 2021. My siblings later joined in, and in June 2023, we started Rezbin, a start-up plastic-waste collection company. By the end of 2023, we had collected almost 2.5 tons of plastics from 18 private companies, 6 schools, and 2 hotels.  Of the three island groups in the Philippines, there are no credited recycling facilities in the Visayas, where we are located. Since our current shredder doesn't have the capacity to shred all the plastics we are collecting, we've partnered with two major recycling companies in the Luzon Island Group to receive and recycle some of the plastic types we've collected (depending on the plastic types they process). Once we are capable, we are hoping to bring in and use other Precious Plastic machines to become a fully credited recycling facility in the Philippines.
data.title: Luvial

data.description: MacKillop Catholic College will become a precious plastic recycling hub. MacKillop will be a community collection point of plastic waste for local schools, businesses, and the wider community. The plastic will be recycled and repurposed into a variety of products such as tables, chairs and building materials. Through this project, we aim to create a culture and legacy at MacKillop of directly contributing to the reduction of plastic waste and its impact on our unique world heritage environment. By creating an interactive plastic recycling hub, we are investing in the education of our younger community and future leaders. Through problem solving, design process and success with their ideas we are enhancing the understanding of scientific and mathematical concepts. These processes are required for future active decision-making and participation in civil, cultural affairs and economic productivity. Furthermore, sustainability and sustainable practices has a stronghold in the Australian Curriculum, and this project would take it beyond the theoretical and into a real-world, practical context.
data.title: MacKillop Community Collective

data.description:
Precious Plastics Liechtenstein is run by the non-profit Makerspace in Liechtenstein. We are a mixed workspace; we shred, extrude and create new products/solutions, providing technological advice, insight into the precious plastics program and creating courses to teach people the importance of the open-source project. We run Precious Plastics as a community space as we are a very tiny nation and we embrace all initiatives that help us spread the word about #preciousplastics. 

We provide a local source of knowledge and develop our workshops to become learning platforms and to be the change our community needs to step away from plastics.

5 Facts you probably didn't know about Liechtenstein:

- We are a tiny nation of 39,000 inhabitants.
- More than half of our landmass is mountains.
- The country is usually referred to as "Liachtaschta", not Liechtenstein, by its citizens.
- The country is not only landlocked but double-landlocked. 

Profile photo by Jan Rozman

data.description: Mama Qucha was born out of our love for the sea and the desire to protect it from plastic bags.  We believe in a plastic-free sea. It is not just a dream, we work every day to make it possible, and our goal is to develop products that allow us all to live sustainably.  We believe that everyone plays an important role and we want to be part of the solution towards sustainable lifestyle changes and a circular economy. In October 2018 we launched the first prototype and in December, our first line with full colour designs. In February 2019 we added social impact: supporting women from Cárceles Productivas. And at the end of the same year we introduced a line of accessories made from 100% recycled plastic bags.  We now work with the Chorrillos Annex Women's Prison and have three product lines. All with the same vision: an ocean free of plastic bags.

data.description: Somos una empresa que se dedica al suprarreciclaje de plástico de un solo uso que se recupera de los alrededores de la Ciénaga Grande De Santa Marta. Creamos productos que son personalizables, funcionales, útiles y sostenibles, siguiendo la estrategia de Economía Circular, el Suprarreciclaje y alineados a los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenibles ODS (9,12,13,14). También ofrecemos MangleTalleres/Charlas/Capacitaciones en  educación ambiental, suprarreciclaje y transformación de residuos, tanto de manera presencial como a través de nuestras redes sociales y medios digitales. Somos una empresa de triple impacto (Social, Ambiental y Económico), que cuenta con el aval de Negocio Verde, verificado por el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible y la Corporación Autónoma Regional del Magdalena (CORPAMAG). Buscamos crear conciencia colectiva de respeto y protección hacia todas las formas de vida, reactivar la economía local del municipio de Pueblo viejo, y dignificar el trabajo de nuestros recuperadores locales.

data.description:
MaraviLixo (WonderWaste) began its research in 2016, shifting uses of discarded materials, taking them as raw materials, through interdisciplinary creative processes that move between design, architecture, fashion and sustainability.
Currently, it develops actions of art and environmental education through workshops and courses, acts in creation and production of sustainability events and constitutes Precious Plastic São Paulo - point of collection and transformation of plastic waste, in addition to a workspace for the construction and use Precious Plastic machines, located in the Bela Vista neighborhood in São Paulo.

A MaraviLixo iniciou sua pesquisa em 2016, deslocando usos de materiais descartados, assumindo-os como matéria prima, através de processos criativos interdisciplinares que transitam entre design, arquitetura, moda e sustentabilidade.
Atualmente, desenvolve ações de arte e educação ambiental através de oficinas e cursos, atua na criação e produção de eventos de sustentabilidade e constitui o Precious Plastic São Paulo - ponto de coleta e transformação de resíduos plásticos, além de um espaço de trabalho para a construção e utilização das máquinas Precious Plastic, situado no bairro Bela Vista, em São Paulo.
data.title: Maravilixo

data.description:
Starting in 2017 and led by Marcela Godoy, Assistant Arts Professor of Interactive Media Arts, this is a place where people gather, share knowledge, and work collaboratively with the purpose of reducing waste and looking into sustainable and innovative solutions to minimize the deterioration of the environment in China. Our hope is that this Re-Makerspace will educate the NYU Shanghai community, as well as Shanghai more broadly, about the plastic pollution problem affecting us as individuals and impacting our micro and macro environments. This is a space where people collaborate to explore innovative ways to transform discarded materials or products into something new and precious, while also seeking sustainable solutions to address social and environmental problems. 

Machines we have:
+ Extrusion
+ Oven and Press
+ Heat Press 
+ PP Shredder
+ Digital fabrication machines (laser cutter, CNC router, woodshop)

data.description:
r•Plastic stand for "recycled plastic". When plastic gets recycled, for example PolyPropylene, the abbreviation changed from PP to rPP. Also when pronouncing r•Plastic it sounds like "our plastic". And thats what we should become aware of: we are responsible, it is all our plastic! We buy it, we use it, we bin it. This realisation gives us great power: we can influence and make change!

r•Plastic stands for playful. The main thing is to have fun and approach live in a playful way. We take it way to serious most of the time! I believe our kids are our greatest teachers and they are most in flow when they have fun!

r•Plastic stands for minimalistic. Don't confuse minimalistic for boring, on the contrary! Minimalistic for us means to be conscious of what we buy and consume. Are the products we buy useful or is it just more stuff? When we create product out of recycled plastic it will be a useful product, it will replace virgin plastic or natural resource, it can be used for many years, it will be recyclable and it will add to a circulair economy. It will be local recycled plastic, the products will be locally produced and offered on the local market.

r•Plastic stands for Tri Hita Karana. This is a Balinees philosophy of life. It boils down to 3 relationships: person to God, person to person and person with nature. All these relationships have to be maintained to achieve harmony and prosperity. This is reflected by r•Plastic in different ways if you pay close attention.
data.title: r•Plastic

data.description:
At Relic we take pride in being recognised as an award-winning micro-manufacturer. Our mission is to make a positive impact by offering exceptional production services using only 100% recycled plastic. We work closely with outstanding designers and businesses who share our vision for a more sustainable future.
  
We specialise in injection moulding, with the ability to produce 10s-1000s of product a month and mix bespoke colourways to your specification - what we call "colour alchemy".
  
We produce sheet material, currently up to 20mm thick and 1000x1000mm in size.

data.description:
Micronesia Climate Change Alliance (MCCA) is a grassroots network of individuals and organizations dedicated to creating community-centered solutions to climate change.

Our network is made up of teachers, students, healers, small business owners and volunteers who seek to build urgency and cohesion through local community projects in order to create a model that is resilient in the face of our changing climate.

Although we are a small team, we have an ambitious agenda to improve the sustainability of our island home by focusing on a wide spectrum of issues such as mitigating and adapting to climate change, transitioning to locally- produced renewable energy sources, promoting food sovereignty, tackling the consumption and waste crisis and advocating for an equitable, just society throughout Micronesia

data.description: My name is Anicet Rakotozafy, 30 years old, and I am a primary school teacher in Switzerland, specifically in Zurich. Currently, I am in my hometown of Antsirabe, Madagascar, addressing local challenges, particularly environmental issues. For the past three months, I've been conducting a kind of on-site study and noticed that plastic waste is a significant problem. There is limited awareness of waste separation, and the city lacks a waste incineration facility.  In addition to this, I plan to tackle additional challenges through a project called "Meet & Create." "Meet & Create" is an educational space for children and teenagers, providing guidance, counseling, access to books, the internet, and sports facilities.  During my research, especially when I discovered Precious Plastic, I realized that "Meet & Create" and Precious Plastic could complement each other as projects. At "Meet & Create," our focus is on Education for Sustainable Development, and I see a promising collaboration between the two initiatives.

data.description:
We believe in a world without new plastic. And we make the best out of the old.
We develop & market sustainable surf equipment and create a new awareness for dealing with plastic through education. We act courageously, authentically and socially.
 
Many people want an alternative to the throwaway society. A conscious and sustainable use of resources such as plastic offers an opportunity to act responsibly and do something good for oneself and the environment. This requires education on recycling and more sustainable products. There is a lack of both. People are looking for practical and attractive ways to use resources more consciously and thus protect themselves and the environment. 
 
Merijaan addresses both problems:
Social: By educating people about up- & recycling, we create a new awareness about how to deal with plastic. We organise plastic recycling workshops and set up circular economies.
Surf: We develop and market sustainable surf equipment made from recycled & recyclable plastic, enabling people to surf in an environmentally and health-friendly way. We use the material that already exists so that no new material is produced.

So far we set up a wole circular economy on Berlin, Alexanderplatz. We collect domestic plastic waste from locals and recycle it into carabiner, soap boxes and rulers, as well as surf related products. 
We have community of more than 70 people and are well connected with all Berlin recycling initatives as well as international ones, especially in Sri Lanka and India.

We work with precious plastic machines, made by Plasticpreneur. Gt in conatct with us if you wish to purchease them - we can help you out.


- Start: in 2019 -> moved to this place in March 2021
- Team: ~3 at the space, but plenty more online (Mould Development, Design and Engineeering) :)
- Machines: We work with all the machines & are happy to experience new ones
- We focus on surf equipment and educational materials. For more info check our website: 
https://merijaan.de/

We are a self-managed social enterprise that since 2015 has impacted thousands of people nationwide and achieved an international reach through the execution of various projects that promote collective environmental awareness and community sustainability. 
We started to work on Precious Plastic Machines since 2017 and to this day we have manufactured over 25 machines, also we work on moulds and products.

data.description:
MobEC - Mobilizing for Circular Economy
We are a community project on Circular Economy, equiped with the set of machines Precious Plastic.
Our aim is to value plastic, allowing to change its perception as a pollutant material to a material that must be used with respect and, giving its extreme versatility, used on a diversity of purposes, from utilitarian to artistic, with economic and social value. The Espaço MobEC (MobEC Space) is stimulated with awareness sessions about Circular Economy in general and specific workshops about plastics and its recovery techniques according to the different types of plastic. The project also develops field trips in different contexts (beach, public spaces and agricultural spaces) where the abandoned plastic will be collected, identified and participants will be led to think about the problematic (from the origin to the end of life) and possible solutions (reverse logistics, reuse, reduction and valuation).
data.title: MobEC

data.description: Together with our partner project in Kayanga started the first plastic recycling center in the very remote area of Northwest of Tanzania in 2022. This project is part of a vocational training center and managed by the catholic diocese of Rulenge-Ngara. It was developed in cooperation with Mojo Fullscale Studio NPO and with support of Sei So Frei and Vulcano from Austria. Until January we were working with a manual plastic shredder and an injection machine developed and produced by plasticpreneur, also from Austria. Recently we added a self-made electrical shredder powered by solar energy. Products are small goods for the local market and for institutions of the diocese (eg. schools, ...). The current portfolio includes abaci, rulers, spinners, hooks, bowls, cups, plates, tiles, clothing pegs, carabiners, buttons and pearls.  In this region is almost no industry and jobs are very rare. This project gives underprivileged people a chance to gain practical skills and an income. We are steadily training staff and building up their abilities to develop and strengthen this project for the goal of a clean environment and a local generated value – out of waste!
data.title: Vulcano Plastic Recycling Center Biharamulo

data.description:
Mother Earth Recycling (MER) is a For-Profit Indigenous Social Enterprise that has been reducing Manitobans landfill contributions since 2012. In the last 5 years, we have diverted 70,000 mattresses, resulting in over 5 million pounds of materials recycled instead of landfilled! We have also collected over 8 million pounds of e-waste for recycling!

At MER, we create meaningful change in the community by providing work based on empathy, compassion, and innovation, for people, the environment, and the local economy.  We hire Indigenous Peoples who are facing multiple personal and systemic barriers, from addictions to homelessness, supportive workplaces are a resource our community needs to thrive. 

On Earth Day 2022 (April 22nd) we will be launching the collection of Child Car Seats for recycling. 59% of the material in car seats is Polypropylene #5 plastic. We have 2 shredders ready and we are building an injection machine. We are hoping to build an extrusion machine and sheet press in the next 12 months. We will be creating new plastic products and have items for sale soon!

Since 2015, Movement France is working in the field of sustainable development in Burkina Faso.
We have set up a project aiming to recycle plastic water-bags, which allows us today to employ 22 young women in our sewing and weaving workshop.
Since 2021, we have decided to further expand our activities, and tackle environmental plastic pollution at a larger scale. We have bought 3 new devices, allowing us to grind and melt plastic, develop our activities, and create new permanent positions among our team

Movement France œuvre depuis 2015 dans le domaine du développement durable au Burkina Faso. 
L'association a mis en place un projet dans le domaine du recyclage des sachets d'eau qui nous permet aujourd'hui à 22 jeunes femmes d'avoir un emploi, grâce à un atelier de couture et de tissage.
Depuis 2021, le souhait de se développer pour lutter contre la pollution de l'ensemble plastique dans l'environnement, a été fait.
Ainsi l'acquisition de 3 machines de broyage et de fonte a permi de développer les activités et de créer des emplois durables localement.

data.description:
The Claro Movement came from an initiative of three friends who share the same ideals: respect for Nature and passion for the Sea. The Claro Movement intends to materialize these ideals in an action that at first sight may seem insignificant and limited, but which can help increase awareness of the problem of plastic in the oceans. This Movement was inspired by a successful campaign by surfers in Cornwall England, but that stems from a global trend towards alerting to the dangers of disposable plastic.

With the success it achieved, the Claro Movement evolved into a Youth Association based in Cascais, in june 2018. It aims to raise awareness of the problem of disposable plastic in the oceans and works on several fronts: it works with the HORECA sector, with companies and its suppliers in the reduction of disposable plastic, also works with the general public by carrying out various awareness activities, carries out educational activities in schools, organizes Eco Cascais, and also works in partnership with the Cascais Town Hall and Cascais Estoril Town Council in projects in this area.
data.title: Movimento Claro

Mudgal Green Initiative Pvt Ltd. is a start-up company, based out of Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India, visioned and founded by two Mudgal brothers who are currently well-settled abroad and want to come back to India to give their best to serve the community. Our vision is to reduce waste going into landfills. Our ultimate goal set up a profitable business model in the Waste Management field in India as it is a neglected and unorganized field and waste is going to be a huge issue for India in the coming decades. 

The company wants to tackle first the plastic waste issue. The plastic waste sector is extremely unorganized and very little information about plastic is known to the community. The reason for us to be here at the Precious Plastic forum is to gather useful knowledge about plastic, current trends, and technological information, so we can give our organization the right direction and start our journey.

UPDATE - 31th of March 2021

-Barrel for Injection machine has been ordered and will be delivered by our machinist next week.
-Heating system for injection machine has been delivered and tested with success.
-Waiting for the barrel delivery to start assembly the Injection Machine.


UPDATE - 25th of March 2021

-Our Shredder has been delivered and we are now Shredding PET, HDPE and PP.

Current activities : 
-Shredding
-3D Design
-3D Print  

Upcoming soon  : 
Injection Molding Machine. (in the next Month)
3D Filament Extrusion Machine. (in the next 3 Months)

The first product we are working on is surf Fins. 
Since we are in a surfing and Kite surfing area, this could be an excellent way to transform the trash for long term use.
This would be the first mold we will have :) 

We are working on designing other future product that will be revealed in the upcoming weeks.



UPDATE - 11th of March 2021

We are now starting a big project to clean Mui Ne (and hopefully Vietnam) from plastic trash.

4 people involved for now- Team might grow in the upcoming weeks. Our workshop is almost ready.

Project includes (non- exhaustive list).
-Collecting
-Recycling
-Transforming single-use object into long term useful ones.
-Branding
-Research and development on material and design.
-Workshops (we target kids first) to 
    -Teach how to be more efficient and how to recycle simple things without needed a factory (starting with plastic bags).
    -Teach how to create valuable items from trash.


The Shredder is on the way (delivery estimated around 25th of March 2021) from a precious plastic machine shop in Saigon (https://community.preciousplastic.com/u/toan-loi-nguyen)


We already work on deigns and prototypes with 3D printing for a while and follow precious plastic project for around 6 years (it was about time to start!).


Other recycling  machines that we are planning to get for our workshop : 


-Injection Machine
-Filament Extrusion Machine (we also have a Chemist in our team - we want to try to develop new polymer materials for 3d print).


Workshop is already equipped with : 
-Basic tools.
-Water pressure washer
-Air Compressor
-MIG Welding machine

More info to come soon.

We make high-quality cruiser skateboards from HDPE.

We are expanding our knowledge base and developing more products and manufacturing techniques.

data.description: This is a community project. The target population will be members of the Rochester community, as well as students and faculty at the local colleges. This project is to translate the blueprints provided by the Precious Plastic network into a materialized technology, and will be the stepping stone for building community involvement, partnerships, and resilience to adversity in addressing issues for sustainability, plastic waste, and climate change. My name is Natasha George, and I am a recent graduate of the Nazareth College of Rochester. I am committed to creating a recycling project in Rochester to build four machines: a shredder, an extruded, an injector, and a compression machine so that plastic of various types can be converted into new products and be sold. Any funds will be used towards establish a workshop, allocating materials for the machines, funding operating an office space, community clean-ups and events, and any other marketing and any other necessary resources to make the project happen. My mission is to eventually turn the organization into a non-profit, and use the proceeds towards the local Rochester community. The mission of this project is to foster community-based collaborating through networking with local groups, non-profits organizations, and businesses in order to implement a new recycling program that can be used on a local scale in the community. This innovation in waste management can close an open cycle to repurposing plastic waste that cannot be effectively processed by recycling centers. I am passionate about this project, because I want to address the challenge of repurposing plastic waste, and I want to give my fellow community members and individuals a new way to participate in the “reduce, reuse, recycle” methods of sustainability. This is important to me, because I believe that because of how much plastic exists in the world, we must find new ways of using it. In this effort, I will encourage stopping plastic pollution and improper sorting while creating new products to be used.
data.title: Natasha George

data.description:
NAUTISURF est une association malouine, de loi 1901, créée en décembre 2015 par le rassemblement de passionnés des sports aquatiques et nautiques (surfeurs, sauveteurs, nageurs) respectueux de leur environnement.

Depuis sa création, l'association participe et organise des actions de nettoyage de plage ainsi qu'une approche sur la problématique des déchets auprès des écoles du Pays Malouin.

Avec Génération Recycleurs, nous voulons montrer au monde la possibilité de transformer, localement, les déchets plastiques en objets du quotidien pour ainsi réduire la pollution et son impact sur l’environnement !
L’objectif est de réduire la demande de nouveaux plastiques vierges et de boucler la boucle en fabriquant des produits durables avec du plastique 100 % recyclé localement.

The aim of the project and business is to go and meet local companies and establish circular economy strategies with them and their employees to reduce their consumption of raw materials.

detail.shortDescription:
We have a plastic shredder and oven on our island Nikoi. If you want to drop off plastic on Bintan, we have an operations base in Kawal. We are company with two Island resorts off the coast of Bintan. As islands we sadly see and collect lots of plastic waste from our beaches daily, which we send off for recycling. Using precious plastic, we have bought a shredder and oven to create plastic moulds, these are both run off the excess solar energy we produce at midday. We will try and sell these items to raise money for the Island Foundation a local children's education charity, and sell them to our guests to raise awareness about plastic pollution. We welcome collaboration so please get in touch.

Kami memiliki mesin penghancur plastik dan oven di pulau kami Nikoi. Jika Anda ingin menjatuhkan plastik di Bintan, kami memiliki basis operasi di Kawal. Kami adalah perusahaan dengan dua resor Pulau di lepas pantai Bintan. Sebagai pulau, kami dengan sedih melihat dan mengumpulkan banyak sampah plastik dari pantai kami setiap hari, yang kami kirim untuk didaur ulang. Dengan menggunakan plastik yang berharga, kami telah membeli mesin penghancur dan oven untuk membuat cetakan plastik, keduanya menghabiskan energi matahari berlebih yang kami hasilkan pada tengah hari. Kami akan mencoba dan menjual barang-barang ini untuk mengumpulkan uang bagi Island Foundation, lembaga amal pendidikan anak-anak setempat, dan menjualnya kepada para tamu untuk meningkatkan kesadaran tentang polusi plastik. Kami menyambut kolaborasi jadi silakan menghubungi kami.

We build machines to remove ocean plastic, specifically microplastics, from the coastlines. We have two machines - a hand powered one and one towed by a quad bike. 
We have now set up a small precious plastic workspace at our workshop. We create phonecases out of the ocean plastic we collect, as well as ghost fishing gear, and other plastic. We turn it into sheets and from there we can create bespoke products :) 
So far we've done medals, sheets, phone cases, golf accessories, buttons, and furniture. 
We're currently upgrading to a much larger sheet press and look to sell 1.5m x 1.5m sheets and ocean plastic tiles.

Drop us a message on Instagram @nurdlecoasts or email through www.nurdle.org.uk and lets work together!

data.description:
New York University Abu Dhabi’s Plastic Recycling Research Lab (aka the Plastic Lab) is an interdisciplinary research lab with a focus on getting and sharing a holistic view on global issues that relate to plastic and plastic recycling. The Plastic Lab was inaugurated in December 2018 by Felix Beck (Assistant Prof. of Practice of Design, NYUAD Engineering Department). He leads the team of dedicated researchers, student research assistants, and community members to work on answers, and develop solutions towards questions such as:

Why plastic? How is plastic produced? How is it used in the market? What are the lifespans of the different types? What are processes of waste collection and processing? What are the short-, mid-, and long-term impacts of plastic waste to the environment? What does plastic recycling mean for todays society? How can recycled plastic be up-cycled into new products? How can the perception of plastic be changed in order to see it as a more precious material instead of a one-time use only material?

Through Precious Plastics, the Plastic Lab focuses on innovative design and outreach to the greater UAE to educate and empower people about recycling and up-cycling.  Through partnerships with other institutions like Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and American University of Sharjah, the NYUAD Plastic Recycling Research Lab hopes to develop a more conscientious and thoughtful consumption culture in the UAE.
data.title: NYUAD Plastic Recycling Research Lab

data.description:
OCTOP'US is a non-profit organization, founded in 2019, based in Strasbourg - operating locally, nationally and internationally. 
Founded by professionals committed to sustainable development and supported by responsible companies, OCTOP'US aims to fight against environmental pollution, especially plastic products, and actively promote the protection of marine biodiversity, as well as aquatic ecosystems. 

To achieve this ambition, OCTOP'US is developing public awareness activities on environmental issues, cleaning operations in France and abroad with the approach on training – recycling methods.

In order to ensure the effectiveness of its actions OCTOP'US promotes the sharing of information and skills between associations and companies involved with ecological transition. 

Finally, supporting Social Solidarity Economy, OCTOP'US promotes creative and innovative actions that share its objectives.
Octop’us concentrates its efforts on activities with clear objectives, such as the development, support and reinforcement of the counseling, informing and forming processes of the target generation, in a European context. These objectives will be met by means of creating the favorable environment in the communities of these young people for the enhancement of their personal and professional performance. Furthermore, their needs will constantly be identified and fulfilled through a large array of sustainable activities.

The association relies on the principles of responsible volunteering, self-motivation and self-determination, active participation (taking initiative, involvement and cooperation) adaptability, continuity, mutual respect and support.)

data.description:
Translating visions into tangible products, Olah Plastic, established in 2018, is a sustainability-focused creative collective from Bandung, Indonesia. Started with making vacuum forming for packaging with a home industry scale and in late 2020, decided to change direction to focus more on recycling, especially plastic. The processed results of plastic waste recycling produce materials that can be categorized into making plastic boards (sheet press) or plastic beams. 

Olah Plastic unites our diverse backgrounds: When arts having an affair with machinery through recycling, processing, and forming. We want to create the best form of sustainable everyday items that are made from recycled packaging or bottles. No need to ask, regardless of its dirty looks, damaged, and lonely in someplace. It's our pleasure to turn plastic waste into something better, as we enchanting the invaluable wasted plastic.
data.title: Olah Plastic

data.description:
We are Precious Plastic Plymouth and Tavistock, a low-tech, artisan plastic recycling project based in Plymouth. 

Our vision is of a world where creative energy drives environmental change.
Our mission is to provide a tool for local recycling and creative engagement to empower the community to live sustainably. We take waste plastic, shred it and re-mould it, using a small injection moulder. 

Currently we can make soap dishes, plant pots and buttons. It is engaging, creative, demonstrates how simple recycling plastic can be and opens up conversations around responsible use of plastic.

I want to recycle plastic to make bricks and have an alternative to build houses in different parts of my country.

data.description: Based in Greater Cleveland, Ohio since 2020. Ohio is the 3rd largest plastics manufacturer the United States. We're proud to be a part of the Precious Plastic community, dedicated to reducing plastic waste and making plastic recycling more accessible and affordable.   ​  Nate Mayfield, who runs FieldCoMfg, builds the machines. So you'll see a Field logo on our machines. He is a machinist, maker and also business owner. Parma Plastics offers a flexible buying and selling experience that caters to your needs, whether you're a small business or hobbyist looking to expand your production capabilities or simply replace old equipment. Our constantly changing inventory includes top brands and models of used machinery, and we can help you find the right machinery at the right time.     We also offer the full line up of Precious Plastic machines that shred, melt, extrude, and compress plastic into new products. Contact us today to discuss your requirements and join us in making a positive impact on the environment by recycling plastic.  ​  We do more than just build and refurbish machines. Check out our Services page to learn what else we can help you with.  ​  Why the Pink Flamingo logo? Our logo, the pink flamingo, is a nod to the local community's obsession with the plastic pink flamingos, which are popular lawn ornaments in our city. While the logo is playful and fun, it's worth noting that there are more plastic flamingos in the world than live, real flamingos. At our company, we're committed to reducing plastic waste and making a positive impact on the environment.
data.title: Parma Plastics

data.description: the cultural association Officine Creative Torino, based in Cecchi Point Hub Multiculturale manage artisan and craftsmanship activities in the cultural programme of the Casa del Quartiere Cecchi Point. At the same time, the association is working at the requalification of the former factory where it is based in. A variety of professionals, in the field of materials, art, design and education constitutes the core team, whose main goals are to protect, promote and innovate the artisan culture and the respect for the environment, through a constant activity of research, experimentation and training. In the space given by the City they gave birth to a community workshop service to provide tools and space for citizens of the district and the city. This service includes a woodshop, a sewing laboratory, welding and metal shop, a bike-mechanics shop and the area lab including the precious plastic experience with the shredder+extruder combo. The users, in DIY or DIWO (do it with others) mode, pay the service economically or in exchange of working hours. Moreover, evening courses and workshops are organized to provide basic training in the different specialties. Last, but not least, special attention is given to junior training, by constantly designing and delivering a conspicuous number of tailored-made labs and events in schools, museums and educational centers of the city for kids and their parents.
data.title: Officine Creative Torino

data.description:
We are a grassroots organization that supports local STEM and Art education based entirely on sustainability. Our principle goal is to work with middle, high school and college students to augment their education. We’re doing this by helping students plan and participate in service opportunities that educate their local communities about sustainability practices. We create innovative items from repurposed plastics to make a dent in climate change!

Our first endeavor in sustainability is the creation of Peninsula Precious Plastics based in San Carlos, California. Students have already begun early community outreach at local museums, parks and their schools. We’ve created a work and collection space that includes a class room and various pieces of Precious Plastics equipment.

data.description:
Hi, im Leon, our recycling work space is "Pewen" Recycling, I recently met Gustavo, he is super interested on Precious Plastic, he is helping and letting me work on his deco-store in the city of San Martin de los Andes, Argentinian Patagonia. 
Two years ago, i started, shy and slowly  to materialize the shredder and the compression machinery. In the beginning i paid this with my daily effort, but i notice it wasn't enough, i took a micro-loan, $10.000 argentinian pesos (not much really), with this i boosted machines up, but the economic devaluation didn't let me finish, meanwhile i teach in schools about plastic recycling, interiorize in plastics, and with the money from teaching i keep the machinery building.
Finally, this year i was able to end the machine building, make it work and make a well done prototype,  automatically the speed reducer gear tear apart, so now we are looking for a new one and focusing on making a beautiful moulds to get profit from the oven and keep researching and developing machines. My endgame: Generate products related with construction, bricks, tiles, beams, etc.
I want a better world for my son and all the beautiful people ( and the ones who are not-so-nice) living here, so, lets recycle!
Hola, yo soy Leon,nuestro espacio de reciclaje es "Pewen" Reciclaje, hace poco conocí a Gustavo, a él le resultó super interesante Precious Plastic, viene ayudando y dejándome trabajar en su espacio de decoración en el Centro de San Martin de los Andes, Patagonia Argentina.
Hace aproximadamente dos años, empecé, tímida y lentamente a materializar la trituradora y el horno compresor.  En principio lo pagaba con mi esfuerzo cotidiano pero al ver que no alcanzaba, saqué un microcrédito de  $10.000 argentinos,  con los que le di un impulso más fuerte a las máquinas, pero la inflación no me dejó terminar, durante ese tiempo empecé a dar clases de reciclaje, con las cuales pagué el resto de las máquinas, me interioricé en el reciclaje. 
Finalmente este año pude terminar de ensamblarlas, ponerlas a funcionar y hacer un prototipo bien terminado, automáticamente el engranaje del reductor de velocidad se barrió, ahora estamos buscando un repuesto y concentrándonos en hacer un molde para empezar a volver redituables a las máquinas y usar ese dinero para seguir creando y construyendo el resto de las máquinas. Mi objetivo final es poder generar productos para la construcción sustentable, como ladrillos, baldosas, vigas, etc.
Quiero un mundo mejor para mi hijo y todas las personas hermosas (y las no tanto) lo habitan, así que, a reciclar!

data.description: Limpho Thoahlane is a dedicated storyteller, expressing her profound narratives through a diverse array of artistic mediums. From photography to film, podcasting to fashion, every creative avenue she explores becomes a canvas for her distinctive voice. At the heart of her artistic journey lies an unyielding commitment to environmental activism. Through her multifaceted work, she not only captivates but also mobilizes her audience towards a shared vision of sustainability.  Over the past three years, Limpho Thoahlane has assumed the mantle of a trailblazer in the realm of Environmental Activism in Lesotho. Her time volunteering at the Hub at Morija and Morija Arts Centre has been transformative, as she spearheads conversations on climate activism and cultivates a culture of proactive discourse. Her influence radiates beyond her personal projects, igniting a passion for action-based dialogue among those she engages with.  With an unswerving dedication, Thoahlane emboldens the youth to embrace their roles as stewards of the environment. Her work is an ardent call to arms, challenging the younger generation to take responsibility for safeguarding our planet and critically assessing their impact. As a result of her efforts, the dialogue surrounding environmental protection has transcended mere conversation and evolved into a call to action.  In her most recent venture, the inception of the plastic recycling company, Pheha Plastic, Thoahlane exemplifies the congruence between her values and her creative endeavors. Through this innovative undertaking, she paints a vivid picture of sustainability by showcasing the transformative potential of single-use plastics. Pheha Plastic not only serves as an emblem of resourcefulness but also seeks to catalyze a shift in consumer behavior within Lesotho.  Through an intricate process encompassing collection, sorting, shredding, and melting, Pheha Plastic breathes new life into discarded materials, reimagining them as exquisite new.

data.description: We are a cultural association (Cas'Aupa) who has decided to bring Precious Plastic to northern Italy. PlasticArt a project that aims at bridging the gap between plastic recycling, arts and crafts, SMEs and creativity in the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region, Italy. We have 2 precious plastic machines (shredder, injector), 1 petbot, and 2 preciousplastic-like machines, that is an extruder and heat press that we have re-adapted for plastic recycling purposes. The project, which receives every year regional fundings, is now at its third edition. The first one, focused on an artistic residence with artists from all over Europe, with a final exposition at our venue. For the second edition, five artists realised Montessori-like toys prototypes. The third edition focuses on realising scene objects for a theatre play with recycled plastic.

data.description:
At plasticiet we’re inspired by the primal beauty of natural stone which we use as the foundation for the visual language of our materials. Alike stone, plastic has an incredible longevity. So instead of wasting it we recycle it by manufacturing beautiful and functional solid surface materials which you can use to realise your project, all the while reducing plastic waste.

Recycled plastics inspired by nature, aspiring to co-create a post waste world. This is what we love to do, and we’re good at it too. Plasticiet was founded in 2018 by Marten van Middelkoop and Joost Dingemans, two Rotterdam based designers with a passion for sustainable material development. We aim to keep challenging the status quo by continuously developing new techniques and create high quality, functional and beautiful materials.

Over the years we have worked with designers, architects, artists, brands and hobbyists resulting in a diverse portfolio of sustainable projects. All our collection as well as bespoke materials are 100% recycled and can be recycled at the end of their lifetime. Find hereunder a collection of projects realized by our customers or ourselves.

data.description: Founded by Javiera Badilla, Rafael Salas and Sebastián Santamaría, LUP is a Chilean design studio that was born at the end of 2014 as part of Javiera and Sebastián's thesis project, with which they sought to extend the useful life of plastic and give value to this type of waste.  We are currently working to bring plastic recycling to communities without access to the traditional recycling chain and to support the development of craftsmanship in these localities. We developed a low-scale recycling system to produce a flexible fibre from plastic waste, called LUP Fibre, which we use to make handmade objects in alliance with craftswomen from different localities, who incorporate this material into their manufacturing processes.  Through this productive link between crafts + design + recycling we seek to increase recycling rates, support local trade and complement the use of vegetable fibres, favouring their regeneration.

data.description:
I have an industrial warehouse with a Shredder Pro and Extrusion Pro in operation.  Currently I have a small team working on product development including surfboard fins and skateboards.  Presently we are producing a variety of plant pots made with HDPE and PP and will be making modular furniture once our plastic supply increases.  Efforts are being made to add a CNC machine to the facility and are looking for a 3D printer partner (of which can be located at my facility).  Currently I am also running the Precious Plastic Kauai Facebook Group and am heading up multiple plastic collection efforts complemented by Hoomalu Ke Kai.  We have collection events during the Old Koloa Town Night Market and the Downtown Lihue Night Market.

Some future products include beach ukuleles, discs for disc golf, and beams for patio furniture.  

In addition to our Precious Plastic machines I've made a refillable activated carbon filter (with activated carbon made from macadamia nut shells from Big Island), a washing station with a closed loop water filtration system, roll around racks to hold bulk bags (I have over 50 of them, so I'd be delighted to have you use them for plastic collection).  The facility also has an oven for pre-heating molds, and a PlasTell plastic identifier.  The team has made molds out of welded plate steel.  The shop consists of plenty of metal working tools for making more steel molds and maintaining them.  We've made a quick disconnect for our Extrusion Pro as well.
data.title: Plastic Paradise

data.description:
Plastic Tactics is a social enterprise that encourages people to be curious about plastic, by getting them hands-on and making useful things themselves from waste plastic, things like plant pots, clothes pegs, and pencil cases.

This gets them thinking more carefully about this precious material - where plastic comes from, how we use it, where it goes when we're done, and what our options are if we're not OK with some of those things.

We are a loose group of volunteers and work in various spaces around Liverpool, UK, developing a community workspace we're calling the Plastic Playground based on Precious Plastic's 40 foot container workspace.

data.description:
The Plastik Kembali philosophy is simple: make cool, usable stuff from plastic waste while doing our part to make the world cleaner, healthier and even more beautiful. Every single day.

---

The Plastik Kembali story started when husband-and-wife founders, Elissa Gjertson & Daniel Schwizer, moved to Lombok, Indonesia in 2018. 

Upon experiencing beaches strewn with waste, rivers clogged with plastic, burning rubbish and more, they knew they wanted to make a difference. 

With research, they discovered PreciousPlastic.com and in 2019, Plastik Kembali (PK) opened its first studio with an oven, some recycled plastic and a passion for art, design & making the world a better place. 

Today, with a larger workspace, an expanded team of local artisans and a unique product line focusing on reimagining traditional Lombok crafts with recycled material, the PK goal is to bring artistic, recycled products to individuals and partners, offering a new solution to the reality of plastic waste in high-tourism areas. And, as always, to clean up the community through meaningful opportunities for artistic expression in the process. 

But most of all, PK hopes to share its core mission with the world: Let’s give single-use plastics a second life … and our planet a second chance.
data.title: Plastik Kembali

data.description: Together with our partner project in Biharamulo we started the first plastic recycling center in the region of Kagera - Northwest of Tanzania in 2022. We developed this workspace in cooperation with Mojo Fullscale Studio and with support of Sei So Frei and fair Styria from Austria. We are working with a manual shredder and an injection machine developed and produced by plasticpreneur, also from Austria. Recently we developed an innovative electrical shredder, operated by solar power. We are producing small goods for the local market for affordable price. So far we are able to produce: abacus, rulers, spinners, hooks, bowls, cups, plates, tiles, clothing pegs, carabiners, buttons, shovels and pearls. This project gives underprivileged people a chance to gain practical skills and an income. We are steadily training our staff and building up their abilities to develop and strengthen this project for the goal of a clean environment and a local generated value – out of waste!

data.description: PlastiX@SAS is an adapted version of a system created by Dutch engineer Dave Hakkens. It aims to produce a variety of products – 3D printer filament to iPhone cases– which have been up-cycled from specific rates of plastic waste that is easily collectible around the Singapore American schools campus. The system's purpose is not only to create meaningful products for trash, but also to act as an advocate for independent, simple up-cycling. data.description:
The Plástico à Vista projet is an environmental awareness project focusing on the problem of plastic as marine litter.

We built a traveling plastic waste mini-station to support awareness actions. We have put together the collective construction methodology of the Ensaios e Diálogos Associação (EDA) with Precious Plastic machines.
We traveled around Trafaria and Costa da Caparica promoting presentation sessions, expert lectures, films, workshops using Precious Plastic machines and sharing information on the problem of climate change.

The population of this coastal territory was able to know the problem of plastic in the world.
We warn of the low awareness of production, consumption and their reuse.

And now, we are looking for new partnerships and investors who want to take this project even further.

This project was co-financed by the European Union and Camões I.P. under the NO PLANET B - AMI project.
data.title: Plástico à Vista

data.description:
ESPAÑOL->
¡Hola!
Somos una Start-up con sede en Medellín Colombia, nuestro propósito es facilitar el trabajo creativo utilizando manufactura aditiva (impresión 3D) + otros procesos convencionales utilizando materiales innovadores y reciclados. Construimos nuestra propia maquinaria, tenemos una trituradora, una inyectora, una mini-extrusora, varias impresoras 3D (las impresoras las compramos, son baratas y confiables) y recientemente compramos una extrusora industrial para tener mayor productividad. Nuestro producto principal es el filamento (insumos) para impresión 3D, sin embargo, creemos fuertemente que el verdadero valor precioso esta en los productos con un diseño de alto impacto. Queremos hacer crecer la comunidad de reciclaje acá en Medellín y sabemos que la mejor manera de crecer es juntos. ¡Necesitamos unirnos para lograr grandes cosas! No dudes en contactarnos nos encanta ayudar así seas nuevo en el tema y apenas estés empezando. 

ENGLISH->
Hi!
We are a Start-up based in Medellín Colombia, our purpose is to facilitate creative work using additive manufacturing (3D printing) + other conventional processes using innovative and recycled materials. We build our own machinery, we have a shredder, an injection machine, a mini-extruder, several 3D printers (we bought the printers, they are cheap and reliable) and we recently bought an industrial extruder to have higher productivity. Our main product is the filament (supplies) for 3D printing, however, we strongly believe that the true precious value is in products with a high impact design. We want to grow the recycling community here in Medellín and we know that the best way to grow is together. We need to come together to achieve great things! Do not hesitate to contact us, we love helping even if you are new to the subject and you are just starting.
data.title: Polymasters

data.description:
We have set up a project on "Plastic recycling" at Hatlab in conjunction with the city of Viroflay and Versailles Grand Parc. A dozen people are active within the association.

The project started in January 2020 and should spread over the whole year.
We should meet twice a month at SunLab or at the town hall of Viroflay.

We plan to build machines and produce useful objects from the second quarter of 2020. Practical workshops will be organized at SunLab in Viroflay, Izylab in Velizy or SQYLab in StQuentin en Yvelines.

======

Nous avons monté un projet sur le "Recyclage du plastique" au Hatlab en lien avec la ville de Viroflay et Versailles Grand Parc. Une dizaine de personnes sont actives au sein de l'association. 

Le projet a démarré en janvier 2020 et devrait s'étaler sur toute l'année. 
Nous devrions nous réunir deux fois par mois au SunLab ou à la mairie de Viroflay.

Nous projetons de construire des machines et de produire des objets utiles à partir du second trimestre 2020. Des ateliers pratiques seront organisés au SunLab de Viroflay, à l'Izylab de Velizy ou au SQYLab de StQuentin en Yvelines. 

En attendant nous organisons des visites en groupe des workshop Precious Plastic en Ile de France ainsi que des sites de recyclage et de transformation du plastique pour monter en compétence.

We are team of 4 enthusiast. Precious Plastic ideas united us in 2018 and we have started annual cleanings in forest area of Bykivnya in Kyiv. We have mastered Shredder, Injection and Extruder and almost finished developing our workspace to present it for society :)

data.description:
Resource Lab is a Open lab that tries to perform experiments in various disciplines which can demonstrate the capabilities of a systems approach. Through these experiments we wish to showcase that solutions to global problems affecting majority of populations already exist and thus question the fact why then are they not being implemented. Our spaces include: Electronic Workshop, Precious Plastic Workshop, Wood Workshop. We are a member in a thriving up cycling community TinkerTank where there is a focus to collect and up cycle the local waste and reprocess the waste locally rather than sending it downstream.. We have setup a collection point for clean label free plastic in cooperation with Orestat Interactive, and currently collect all the types of plastic and shred on site. The precious plastic workshops consists of the shredder , oven, injection and extrusion machines. Fell free to get in touch via message and make sure to drop by to give us your clean label free plastic. Tak


In the spirit of the precious plastic we don't believe in intellectual property thus any collaborations or  creation through the use of our lab has to be Free and Open Source.

Showing how to work with plastic sourced from everyday trash. We work together with the Technical University Harburg and different social projects in Hamburg. Next years plan is to find a new workshop to really start on the teaching and having workshops. 

Everybody is welcome to join our group and help us build awareness about the plastic problems in Hamburg and worldwide.

data.description: We build a community in Los Angeles & around the world interested in solving the plastic pollution problem through recycling plastic and DIY solutions. We got a kick start in funding thanks to Parley for the Oceans and Adidas hiring us to bring machines out for live event activations at their Run for the Oceans events and their large NBA All Star weekend event/concert. We continue to do event activations periodically. We are a non-profit that is loosely organized and is more of a do-ocracy where we like to empower anyone who is motivated and passionate to do and build what interests them. We have built a shredder, a couple injectors that we loan out to local organizations and schools trying to get started with plastic recycling. And, we have done lots of tests with recycling plastic with toaster ovens, paper shredders and other DIY creations. A few times a year we host demo days to bring everyone in Southern California interested in Precious Plastic together to network, trade stories and to help each other out. Currently our 'workspace' is at Richard Wilks's Studio at The Brewery near Downtown LA, but we have many members that have different workshops, workspaces, or their home garage where they do some level of plastic recycling.

data.description: We are the oldest continuously operating Precious Plastic shop in the Philippines.  With 8 full time employees, we build all the Precious Plastic machines, as well as design and make molds, conduct research projects and do molding projects.Our shop uses modern fabrication techniques to include fiber laser cutting, waterjet, CNC bending, MIG welding and CAD.  We have one engineer on staff.  We supply Precious Plastic machinery to NGO's to include the UN, WWF, Rotary, among others.  We also are registered for Philippines government procurement and supply plastic shredders to many local government waste management facilities. Our Precious Plastic machines are in use from the farthest north parts of Luzon to the farthest south part of Mindanao with hundreds of plastic shredders fabricated.  We work with the International Coastal Cleanup and other NGO to convert ocean plastic into new products.We also host foreign volunteers for Precious Plastic via Workaway.  If you are interested in volunteering with us, let us know.  We have hosted visiting engineers from Denmark, Netherlands and South Africa to date.

data.description: This is an exciting environmental education project and artisan recycling facility. We are a team combining educators, scientists, artists, play leaders and other eclectic contributors. We are based at Ocean Studios in the Royal William Yard, Plymouth, thanks to  the Real ideas Organisation https://realideas.org/, Start Something initiative. With our engaging machines we are able to take waste plastic shred and re-mould it into useful products. We engage through demonstrations, workshops and educational resources taking a playful, creative approach but delivering a strong environmental message. This is to encourage reduction and recycling of plastic waste and ensure that plastic does not enter the oceans. Plymouth, UK, is a coastal city. The university is known worldwide for ground-breaking research on marine micro-plastics and the city has strong environmental groups working to reduce marine litter. We provide informative resources explaining which plastics are recycled by Plymouth City Council, where other plastics can be recycled, alternatives to plastic packaging and myth busting around recycling. We have designed a cartoon character, Dr Dot, who helps us to deliver our messages she is an engaging, eco-warrior and glamorous scientist, a great role model for kids, particularly girls.
data.title: Precious Plastic Plymouth and Tavistock

data.description:
At Precious Plastic Santa Maria we focus on flexible plastics such as packaging from the food industry and plastic bags (still given for free in abundance in grocery stores). We use the technique of melting the plastic with an iron as well as transforming plastic without the need of this process, shining a light on plastics that are not easy to melt. In Santa Maria there are many talented artisans and designers that love to stitch with sewing machines, so we focus on the creation of what we call "plastic fabrics". 

We then take these unique fabrics and create precious products that range from fanny-pack (waist bags), eco bags, rain coats, flowers pots, wallets and so on. We thrive to help the city to transition towards a circular economy and have the mission to expand our network of partners with local business, generating awareness in the city and helping companies to be more sustainable by being aware of the precious plastic waste they currently generate. 

We believe that together we can create a beautiful future for our city, inspiring cities arround us and sharing what we learn with the world :)
data.title: Precious Plastic Santa Maria

data.description:
We are a small team that got together in August 2019 to set up a multi purpose work space, to develop new and improved ways to work with recycled plastic and to create new and better products. 

We are also a member of and support Rethink Recycling Co-op

As well we are a waste materials and sustainability education center dedicated to help re-educate the community from primary school to industry with our developing industry leading mobile educational program run in partnership with Rethink Recycling and Precious Plastic Monash Uni.

We have 200sqm facility with a V4 extruder, 2 x V4 pro shredders, a 900x900 sheet press production line and a pneumatic injection machine, a classroom for learning or study and a full suite of tools to compliment any project you are working on. 

We also offer for sale a large range of processing machines, from desk top hand cranked versions to fully automatic semi industrial ones all made to Australian safety and electrical standards. 

We also have a supply of clean ground plastic, and can grind your own plastic for you. Contact us for more details

CNC aluminium moulding for injection, extrusion and compression systems are also part of what we can do for you. We also have a laser when detail is required. Get in touch and let us know how you want to get involved and we can help you start your recycling journey.

As a company we want to help educate the community on the 8 R's and create a hub to unite the greater community to live and work a better way.

RETHINK your choices
REFUSE single use
REDUCE consumption
REUSE everything
REFURBISH old things
REPAIR before you replace
REPURPOSE be creative, reinvent
RECYCLE as the last option


We are located at 21 Aspen Circuit, Springvale, Victoria, Australia.
data.title: Precious Plastic Victoria

Precious Plastic Manyatta is a Team on a mission to ensure everyone gets to refuse, reduce, reuse or recycle plastic waste. The Team holds monthly sensitization and awareness campaigns on plastic waste recycling and environmental conservation within the locality, educational institutions, and with organizations. Also, participating in environmental conservation events organized by other conservationists like Kisumu environmental champions.

Precious Plastic Manyatta collects plastic waste for its recycling workshop directly and, by collaborating with other institutions generating plastic waste. The Team also buys plastic waste from independent collectors who are paid some incentive for their initiative. Plastic is then cleaned and sorted into different plastic categories ready for shredding and production.

data.description: The Precious Plastic UFPB is a creative recycling space that combines design, economics, carpentry, urban planning, and other sustainability-related practices. This space is affiliated with @maressemplastico, an institutional project of the Federal University of Paraíba that has been taking actions against sea waste in the state since 2019. Focused on the circularity of plastic, we believe in the possibility of reintegrating plastic waste removed from coastal environments by creating projects that meet the community's needs. In our laboratory, we have a multidisciplinary team working on manufacturing plastic boards for making urban furniture, educational games, and other objects. We also conduct educational activities in communities, such as training workshops for children and young people. With a focus on continuous process and material improvements, we establish partnerships and strengthen ties with other organizations and educational institutions. These connections enable researchers, professionals, and students to participate as an extension of their academic practices, testing processes, cataloging materials, and developing production methods that can evolve into new products and services.
data.title: Precious Plastic UFPB

data.description:
I am the Co-founder and Manager for the Female Assistant Initiative Towards Help Inc. FAITH Inc. is a Liberian registered NGO engaged in humanitarian activities, sanitation, and plastic waste collection in various counties of Liberia. The organization has over two hundred volunteers and its’ objective is to identify with government, the international community, and other local and international entities in making all of Liberia clean, safe, and beautiful-complete protection of the environment. One of our major and current activities is plastic waste recycling keeping with both national and global aim to find solutions to plastic pollutions.

 There is only one company (SETHI BROTHERS-DURA PLAST), that is engaged in plastic recycling in the whole Country (Liberia), and we are the only organization that serve as the highest supplier of plastic waste to them. Sadly, the company is selective in her choice of plastic waste. Therefore, as organization, our objective to free our environment from plastic pollution is far from being reached if nothing is done to address the situation. We believe our partnership with Precious Plastic will bring about lasting solution to our massive plastic waste.

However, our goal is not only to work with plastic but also wide view for all the garbage materials. Our main source of plastic waste collection its from Sao Paulo, the biggest city of Brazil, and also from its beaches, plus from donations of people that collaborate with the project.

Our biggest challenge is to keep this business profitable, however not because we are looking for gain a lot of profits, but for maintain and grow the S.I.R.I.

We hope you like our work and let's REPLASTIC everything together!!

data.description:
Rodrigo Oliveira worked with solid waste disposal engineering projects when he realized that the amount of recyclables being buried in landfills was impressive. Unfortunately, 75% of Brazilians do not separate recyclable material and municipal selective collection affects only a small part of the population, according to a survey conducted by Ibope in 2018. In addition, Rodrigo was aware that most recyclable recovery in Brazil was carried out by informal workforce without guaranteed labor rights.Faced with this reality, while pursuing his master’s degree in sustainability in 2016, Rodrigo came across the concept of urban mining – the process of locating and retrieving useful elements of discarded items for reuse. He decided to do this by formalizing the work of former waste pickers.Then came the partnership with Adriano Leite and Leandro Metropolo, who worked with technology, to develop post-consumer packaging tracking software. Together, the 3 of them launched Green Mining, which in 2018 was one of the 21 startups selected by Ambev Brewery 100+ Accelerator from all around the world. This AB InBev initiative in partnership with the UN Global Compact seeks small and medium-sized entrepreneurs with innovative proposals for some of today’s key social and environmental issues.In December, Rodrigo, as a representative of Green Mining, received a congratulation called “Vote of Jubilation” from the São Paulo City Council in recognition of the initiative launched. Ambev’s President (Bernardo Paiva) and Sustainability Vice-President (Rodrigo Figueiredo de Souza) were also awarded.

In February 2019 came the 1st international award: Green Mining was in the Top 3 of the “Better World Award”, held in Belgium. In October won the Climate Ventures Green Business Ideas Competition, which enabled the startup to represent Brazil on the worldwide Climate Launchpad program in Holland.
data.title: Green Mining

data.description:
Given the excessive presence of unused plastic waste in my commune, my initiative was born.
This goes beyond promoting care for the environment. For planning and organization, we are using only PP (polypropylene) and / or HDPE (high-density polyethylene) waste; all this, to take it to a process of transformation to raw material. The waste is found in municipal recycling points, voluntary contributions, door to door and
own work, -initially using- a bicycle cart as a means of transport, capturing the
people's attention, spreading the word and gaining collective recognition. After the
collection, the selection of the material is carried out (by type and color); then crushed (using
Crushing machine); washing (only with water); extrusion / casting of the material (with extruder machine)
and finally the production of raw material with the use of molds.

data.description:
(EN)

Where many see waste, we see opportunities // Stuttgart - Lima

We are a non-profit organization founded in Germany by seven peruvians. Our initiative was born from the idea of implementing an inclusive and accessible recycling center in Lima, in order to increase levels of household waste segregation and provide new tools to urban waste pickers to improve their quality of life.

With our project "#NoComasPlastico" we bring collectors from the district of Comas, Lima to the range of possibilities that exist to give value to plastic waste. We have started with a small workspace where the shredder and injection maschine work first of all for educational activities in collaboration with the environmental education team led by the municipality of Comas.
A next phase of the project includes the production and promotion of a new product in collaboration with a group of local collectors. Follow up our adventure!!!

Donde muchos ven residuos, nosotros vemos oportunidades // Stuttgart - Lima

Somos una organización sin fines de lucro fundada en Alemania y conformada por siete peruanos. Nuestra iniciativa nació de la idea de implementar un centro de reciclaje inclusivo y accesible en Lima, con la finalidad de incrementar niveles de segregación de residuos domésticos y brindar nuevas herramientas a los recolectores urbanos para mejorar su calidad de vida.

Con nuestro proyecto "#NoComasPlastico" acercamos a recolectores del distrito de Comas, Lima al abanico de posibilidades que existen para darle valor a los residuos plásticos. data.description: Precious Plastic ReciclAMAR began its journey in the sustainable world by turning plastic waste into valuable products in the year 2023. Our workspace is an innovative hub located within the extension of the IFRN-CNAT, where we invite passionate individuals to collaborate and contribute to a greener future.  Our dedicated team comprises a diverse group of creative and technical minds, currently standing at ten members, all committed to reducing plastic waste and fostering a culture of sustainability. In collaboration with Precious Plastic Cotia in Brazil, we have equipped our workspace with essential machines such as the shredder, the injection, and the oven. These tools allow us to transform discarded plastic into a variety of products, enhancing both the value and the lifecycle of the material. Our product line is constantly evolving, but currently includes keychains, containers, plates, tangram sets, and more. We pride ourselves on our creativity and the ability to innovate new items daily, ensuring that we're always bringing fresh and functional products to the market. In addition to product creation, our group is actively involved in educational and community outreach activities to promote recycling and environmental awareness.
data.title: Precious Plastic ReciclAMAR

data.description: Re=Comb was founded by Sarah Jo Palmer and Christopher Deagle, hair stylists who have worked with some of the biggest names in the fashion industry. Their extensive experience lead them to rethink environmental impact of the fashion industry, and have become passionate about finding solutions to reduce waste and promote sustainability.  Re=Comb is the embodiment of their mission to change the future of hair tools and start an eco-movement to help change the hair industry’s future.  Plastic waste is a big problem, with enough plastic thrown away every year to circle the world 5 times. Shockingly, only 9% is recycled, causing huge environmental damage.   RE=COMB gives waste a new life, reducing landfill and ocean waste. “At Re=Comb, we believe that we all have a responsibility to take care of our planet. By reducing our plastic consumption, stopping single-use plastic, and reusing and recycling what we can, we can all make a difference.” RECYCLE with RE=COMB We recycle PP 5 HDPE 2 & LDPE 4 Connect with us at Info@re-comb.com   REDUCE REUSE RECYCLE.

Recyclage Plastique Maison est une jeune association Valaisanne qui prend part à Precious Plastic. Composée d’un groupe de jeunes étudiants motivés à faire bouger les choses, cette association est en constante évolution !
Cette association a pour but de recycler le plastique pour lui donner une deuxième vie. Elle propose déjà de nombreux produits : porte-clés, dessous de verre, cadres photos, formes décoratives, lettres pour prénom et plus encore !
Recyclage Plastique Maison participe activement à la vie publique ! En mai 2021, elle est venue présenter son projet lors du festival Alternati’Valais à Sion, mais aussi en décembre 2021 auprès des plus jeunes lors du marché de Noël de la capitale. Ses buts ne sont donc pas seulement de recycler les nombreux plastiques du quotidien, mais aussi de sensibiliser petits et grands autour d’ateliers et de discussions 

Recyclage Plastique Maison is a young Valaisan organisation who participate to the movement Precious Plastic. Composed of a group of young and motivated students, this association tries its best to change things. It is in constant evolution! The goals of RPM are to recycle plastics by giving them a second chance. RPM has developed a wide range of products, such as key-charms, coasters, photo frame, decorations, and many more!
The organisation takes actively part to the public life! In May 2021, it presented its project during the festival of Alternati'Valais in Sion, and also in December 2021 during the Christmas market of the capital city. RPM does not only wants to recycle plastics, but also to raise awareness of people of all ages during work sessions and discussions.
